article.articleHeadline: RDC/Ebola : l'épidémie reste incontrôlée malgré une baisse nationale (OMS)
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC/Ebola: the outbreak remains out of control despite a national decline (WHO).
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) remains uncontrolled as of 20 September 2026, despite a modest national decline in cases. The World Health Organization (WHO) Africa regional office reports 7,733 confirmed cases and 3,732 deaths. Transmission is increasingly dispersed geographically, with the latest expansion in the Dungu health zone in Haut-Uélé Province, near the border with South Sudan, raising cross-border transmission risk. Since the outbreak began, 63 health zones across seven provinces have been affected. The WHO classifies national risk as very high and neighboring land-border countries as high. This outbreak is the largest and deadliest ever recorded in the DRC and the second-largest globally after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. The report provides no further details on infection sources or clinical symptoms.

triage.headline_ja: DRC/エボラ：全国的な減少傾向にもかかわらず、流行は依然制御不能（WHO）
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模のエボラ流行が継続し、致死率約48%、越境（南スーダン）リスクを伴う地理的拡大が見られるためIHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: スーダン・アンゴラは発生地域として記載されているが、記事本文では越境リスクの言及のみで実際の発生国はDRCのみ。両国は対象国リストにも含まれないため verified_locations から除外。

article.articleHeadline: தொற்று நோய் பரவல்: சுகாதாரத்தை மேம்படுத்த அரசுக்கு வணிகர்கள் ஒத்துழைக்க வேண்டும் - விக்கிரமராஜா வேண்டுகோள்
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Spread of infectious diseases: Merchants should cooperate with the government to improve public health — Vikramaraja's appeal.
article.articleSummary: As Tamil Nadu's monsoon season begins, dengue fever, typhoid, and yellow fever–like mosquito- and water-borne diseases are spreading rapidly, according to a statement by A. M. Vikramaraja, president of the Confederation of Tamil Nadu Traders’ Associations. He urges merchants to display awareness posters in shops to educate customers and promote public health. The appeal underscores the need for active cooperation with the government to curb transmission and protect shoppers during the wet season. The emphasis is on awareness, early recognition of symptoms, and prompt reporting, though no case counts are provided. The call to action focuses on routine public health messaging in commerce venues across Tamil Nadu to mitigate vector- and waterborne disease risks during the monsoon.

article.articleHeadline: Waspada "Superflu" pada Anak, Influenza A Subklad K Bukan Flu Biasa
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Watch Out for 'Superflu' in Children: Influenza A Subclade K Is Not the Ordinary Flu
article.articleSummary: Influenza A subclade K, nicknamed 'Superflu', has spread to at least 13 Indonesian provinces, increasing influenza activity with a notable impact on children. As of week 36 of 2026 (early September), influenza cases rose from 35% to 46% week over week, with 42% of detections in the 0–4 year age group. Laboratory confirmation via throat swab is needed to distinguish influenza from other respiratory viruses. In children, symptoms include high fever (39–40°C), severe myalgia, headache, and fatigue; warning signs are fever >39°C, dehydration, rapid or labored breathing, and signs of pneumonia—seek prompt care. H3N2 Subclade K is detected in 13 provinces, most in East Java, South Kalimantan, West Java, and DKI Jakarta. Indonesia remains dominated by H1N1pdm09 among influenza A, but antivirals are reserved for severe cases and antibiotics are not useful; vaccination for all children >6 months is recommended, with reinforced preventive measures (hygiene, cough etiquette, ventilation).

triage.headline_ja: 小児の「スーパーフル」に警戒を、インフルエンザA亜系統Kは通常のインフルエンザではない
triage.triage_reason: H3N2亜系統『K』という新興株がインドネシア13州に急速に拡大し、特に0-4歳児で重症化サインを伴う症例が増加しているため、IHR基準（重大性・異常性）とWPRO基準（重症度・流行しやすさ）を複数満たす。
triage.notes: H3N2亜系統Kはインドネシア13州（東ジャワ、南カリマンタン、西ジャワ、DKIジャカルタ中心）で検出され、小児（0-4歳）に42%の症例が集中。重症化サイン（高熱、脱水、呼吸困難、肺炎兆候）が報告されているが、死亡例や医療逼迫の具体的データは記事に記載なし。国際的な拡大や渡航制限の情報は不明のため、続報の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization: Ebola outbreak in the Congo remains out of control - Urdu Point
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains out of control, according to the World Health Organization, despite slight declines in cases. By 23 September 2026, there are 7,733 confirmed Ebola cases and 3,732 deaths, with transmission reaching 63 health zones across seven provinces. The outbreak has reached Dungu Health Zone in Haut-Uele Province, near the South Sudan border, increasing cross-border risk. About two-thirds of recent deaths occurred outside health facilities, indicating delays in detection and care. Domestic risk is very high and regional risk high. Declared in May, this is the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the DRC’s history and the second-largest globally after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic.

article.articleHeadline: 市公卫临床中心获评国家传染病医学中心"HIV快速启动抗病毒治疗区域示范中心"
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Municipal Public Health Clinical Center Named National Center for Infectious Disease Medicine "Regional Demonstration Center for Rapid Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy for HIV"
article.articleSummary: Municipal Public Health Clinical Center has been named a National Center for Infectious Disease Medicine Regional Demonstration Center for Rapid Initiation of Antiretroviral Therapy for HIV, one of 13 nationwide. Emphasizing the motto 'early detection, rapid start, early treatment,' the center advances standardized HIV care with a streamlined, one-stop pathway for screening, referral, diagnosis and treatment in collaboration with disease-control authorities. The designation centers on rapid ART initiation—on the day of diagnosis and within seven days—alongside guideline adherence and treatment success as core performance indicators, illustrating effective medical–epidemiologic collaboration and quality-control across the care continuum. The accolade marks a milestone in high-quality infectious diseases development. Future work includes expanding the regional model through infection and immunology clinics, strengthening CDC partnerships, refining workflows and quality standards, and promoting regional academic exchanges and technical support to elevate HIV care nationwide.

triage.headline_ja: 市公衛臨床センターが国家伝染病医学センター「HIV迅速抗ウイルス治療開始地域模範センター」に選出

triage.notes: 記事はHIV治療体制の整備・表彰に関する内容であり、新規感染拡大等のシグナルは認められない。

article.articleHeadline: 宿迁农村地区"一老一小"流感疫苗免费接种工作启动
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In the rural areas of Suqian, the free influenza vaccination program for the elderly and young children has begun.
article.articleSummary: Rural Suqian, Jiangsu Province, has launched a free influenza vaccination program for the elderly (65+) and primary/secondary school students as part of the 2026–2027 season. On Sept 21, at the Suqian Economic Development Zone Huanghe Street Health Service Center, 70-year-old Cao Dianju became the first recipient. The program provides one dose of the trivalent inactivated influenza vaccine (split-virion) to eligible rural residents. It follows a national joint notice by the National CDC and eight departments, targeting the rural 'one old, one young' group to reduce influenza infections and severe outcomes. Vaccination is encouraged from September to October, with protection developing 2–4 weeks after inoculation. Eligible individuals should bring ID and household registration; those with fever or contraindications should postpone. The vaccine supply is adequate and regulated; non-free groups may access discounts, including a 'two people, one free' promotion. Authorities will maintain oversight and public education.

article.articleHeadline: Waspada, Influenza A Meningkat di Jabar, IDAI Beberkan 3 Petunjuk Emas Bagi Orang Tua
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Be vigilant, Influenza A on the rise in West Java, IDAI reveals 3 golden tips for parents.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A cases among children are rising in West Java, according to IDAI Jawa Barat. The Indonesian Pediatric Society warns parents to monitor three golden indicators: activity, intake, and output, as fever alone does not determine severity. Typical Influenza A symptoms include abrupt high fever (38–40°C), dry cough, sore throat, severe muscle pains, and marked fatigue. Since children may not express discomfort, caregivers should watch for changes in activity, hydration, and urination, aiming to keep fluids up and checking urine output roughly every four hours. Seek emergency care if warning signs appear: difficulty waking, altered or agitated behavior, seizures, rapid breathing, blue-tinged skin, bleeding, or no urine for six hours. The guidance emphasizes prevention of serious complications beyond respiratory symptoms.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization says the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains out of control.
article.articleSummary: WHO says the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains out of control, despite a slight nationwide decline in cases. As of Sunday, the country has 7,733 confirmed cases and 3,732 deaths, according to WHO Africa Region. The outbreak’s footprint is expanding geographically—now 63 health zones across seven provinces—with the Dungu Health Zone in Haut-Uele near the South Sudan border marking the latest expansion and raising cross-border transmission risk. In North Kivu, treatment facilities are strained, with standard-care bed occupancy at 91.2% and 34.2% of patients treated outside these facilities. Two-thirds of recent deaths occurred outside health facilities, reflecting delays in detection and access to care. Declared in May, this is the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the DRC’s history and the second-largest globally after the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak.

article.articleHeadline: Kemenkes Ungkap Sebaran Kasus Influenza di 38 Provinsi, Jawa Timur Tertinggi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Health Reveals Distribution of Influenza Cases in 38 Provinces, East Java Has the Highest.
article.articleSummary: Influenza surveillance in Indonesia shows a rise in the proportion of positive influenza specimens to 51% in week 36 of 2026, up from 37% in week 35, with the A(H1N1)pdm09 subtype currently dominant. Despite the uptick, national influenza activity remains categorized as low and is considered under control. ILI cases are highest in East Java, Central Java, and West Java, with children under five years old accounting for 41.9% of influenza cases, based on SKDR data through week 36 updated September 19, 2026. To monitor the situation, authorities are strengthening ILI and SARI surveillance, expanding RT-PCR testing and viral genome monitoring, and increasing traveler surveillance at points of entry to detect potential viral changes and track trends.

article.articleHeadline: Brazilian Agroforests Harbor Surprising Mosquito Diversity and Disease
article.articleSummary: Three-year study (2022–2025) at Terra Boa Farm, Silva Jardim, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil documented 5,314 immature mosquitoes from 38 species. Culex dominated (53.8%), followed by Limatus (16.6%) and Wyeomyia (16.2%); five species—Cx. iridescens, Cx. pleuristriatus, Lim. durhamii, Wy. edwardsi, and Ae. albopictus—made up about 80% of captures. Natural habitats (bromeliads, bamboo internodes, peach palm bracts) yielded 4,175 specimens (78.6%) and 34 species, with 26 exclusive to natural sites; bromeliads produced 2,031 individuals from 22 species. Bamboo internodes were dominated by Cx. iridescens (72.4%) and harbored Toxorhynchites trichopygus larvae. Artificial containers (tarps and a 200-L barrel) held 1,139 specimens from 12 species, led by Li. durhamii and Ae. albopictus (tarps 83.7%). Cx. quinquefasciatus appeared in tarps; sylvatic yellow fever vectors Haemagogus leucocelaenus/janthinomys and Sabethes identicus were found in bamboo near Poço das Antas reserve, signaling spillover risk and the ecological plasticity of vectors in agroforestry, with Ae. albopictus as a generalist.

triage.notes: 本記事はリオデジャネイロ州の農林複合地域における蚊の種多様性調査に関する学術的研究で、黄熱病媒介蚊（Haemagogus属等）の存在が確認されたことでスピルオーバーリスクの可能性が指摘されているが、実際のヒト感染事例や発生報告はない。ブラジルは対象国リストに含まれるが、実際の疾病発生（アウトブレイク）ではなく生態学的調査のため、verified_locationsは空とした。

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Remains Uncontrolled: WHO
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak remains uncontrolled as of 23 September 2026, with transmission increasingly geographically dispersed and moving toward an international border, adding strain to response capacity. The country has reported 7,733 confirmed Ebola cases and 3,732 deaths as of 23 September 2026, according to the WHO African regional office via Xinhua. Declared in May, this outbreak has become the largest and deadliest Ebola event ever recorded in the DRC and the second-largest globally, after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. Despite a modest nationwide decline in infections, transmission persists and shifts across regions, and sustained geographic expansion is cited by the WHO as a major challenge to containment and resource allocation.

triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれるが、記事サマリーはDRC国内の流行拡大と国境への接近について述べているのみで、Angolaでの発生を明示していないため除外した。DRC史上最大・最悪のエボラ流行であり、2014-2016年西アフリカ流行に次ぐ規模。

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: District magistrate's directive to increase HIV infection testing.
article.articleSummary: Chamrajanagar district launches an HIV/AIDS testing drive under a Mobile AIDS Safety campaign, with District Magistrate Srirupa directing officials to urge youth to self-test. An inter-department meeting announced an app with HIV testing details, locations, and confidential counseling, plus a QR code. Posters will be displayed in schools and colleges. Government hospitals will conduct HIV screening at the primary level; confirmed cases receive free treatment at Mysuru’s SIMS and Kollegal SDH. ART is emphasized to enable healthier living; high-risk groups will be identified and tested, including students, mining and quarry workers, industrial workers, tribals, and interstate-border drivers; local panchayats, police, and NGOs will cooperate. Under the National TB Elimination Programme, TB awareness and services are strengthened: India accounts for about 25% of global TB cases, with around 1,200 annually in the district; Gundlupete lowest, Hanur highest. In 2025, 55 gram panchayats were TB-free; more to come. KSAPS posters released.

article.articleHeadline: Apa Itu Influenza A? Virus Flu Paling Berbahaya yang Kini Ditemukan di Jawa Barat
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: What Is Influenza A? The Most Dangerous Flu Virus Now Found in West Java
article.articleSummary: Influenza A is described as a highly transmissible, dangerous influenza virus currently raising concerns in West Java amid a surge of respiratory illnesses. Influenza A infections present with sudden high fever (38–40°C), dry cough, sore throat, severe muscle pain, and marked fatigue, unlike mild colds. Subtypes circulating in humans include H1N1 and H3N2. Experts highlight three main reasons it is considered more dangerous than influenza B or C: rapid mutation via antigenic drift and shift, cross-species transmission enabling zoonotic spillover from birds and pigs, and potential to drive global pandemics. Vulnerable groups—children, the elderly, and those with comorbidities—face higher risks of complications such as pneumonia, neurological disorders, and organ failure. IDAI West Java chair Prof. Anggraini Alam urges parents to monitor three golden indicators in children: activity level, fluid intake, and urine output, noting that fever alone is not a safe safety barometer. Monitoring helps early detection.

triage.headline_ja: インフルエンザAとは何か？西ジャワで発見された最も危険なインフルエンザウイルス
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はインフルエンザA全般に関する一般的な医学解説・啓発記事であり、特定の異常なアウトブレイクや具体的な症例数の増加を報じるものではない。

article.articleHeadline: Rat-bite incident: HC orders joint inspection of Trichy GH
article.articleSummary: Rat-bite incident at Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Government Hospital (MGMGH), Trichy, prompts the Madras High Court to order a joint inspection by the hospital dean and the Trichy Corporation Commissioner. The division bench also directs the district collector to coordinate the inspection and assess compensation feasibility for 68-year-old R Tamilkodi; case adjourned to October 15. Tamilkodi, diabetic, was bitten on the left toe by a rat on July 21 while recovering in a general ward after surgery for a leg fracture the day before. Her family had alerted authorities about rat infestation three days earlier. An advocate team found sanitation lapses: poorly maintained toilets (broken/missing doors), inadequate cleaning and water facilities, sewage leakage, stagnant drainage water, open drains near wards, rodent access, and roaming stray dogs. Counsel warns stagnant water could breed vectors such as mosquitoes, heightening risks of dengue, malaria, and secondary bacterial infections.

article.articleHeadline: 中秋国庆双节将至，中疾控提醒防范诺如、新冠等传染病
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: As the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays approach, China CDC reminds people to guard against norovirus, COVID-19, and other infectious diseases.
article.articleSummary: Published 2026-09-23, the China CDC issues health tips for the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays, noting increased travel and gatherings. Guidance: check destination outbreak info, ensure vaccination, and take anti-mosquito measures; maintain regular sleep and avoid late nights or overeating. Norovirus gastroenteritis is a major foodborne risk; transmission via contaminated food/water or contact with vomit or feces, with outbreaks common in tour groups. Prevention includes frequent handwashing, avoiding raw water, cooking shellfish thoroughly, and using chlorine-based disinfectants with disposable gloves for vomit. For respiratory infections, influenza and COVID-19 risks rise in crowded places; wear masks if symptomatic, cover coughs, and ventilate homes 2–3 times daily. Dengue, chikungunya, and Zika threaten travelers to Southeast Asia, Africa, and South America; returners should monitor for 14 days. Also beware fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, monkeypox, cholera, Ebola, and other zoonoses; avoid ticks and unknown animals; seek rabies vaccination after bites.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Coast Guard busts illegal import of prohibited veterinary drugs; the suspect even used Andy Lau's name to smuggle Chinese avian influenza vaccines.
article.articleSummary: As of 23 September 2026, Taiwan’s Coast Guard and a multi-agency task force intercepted 93.6 liters of illegal avian influenza vaccine from mainland China, concealed in yogurt and intended for the domestic poultry industry. A man surnamed Chen used the alias 'Andy Lau' as the consignee to evade detection in two unauthorized orders. The operation, involving Yunlin Coast Guard Investigation Team, Taoyuan and central-southern coast patrols, the 13th Coast Guard Fleet, Yunlin Police Bureau, Customs Administration, and the Council of Agriculture’s quarantine bureau, resulted in Chen’s arrest and seizure of all illicit vaccine. Authorities estimate the quantity could immunize about 100,000 poultry; the case is prosecuted under the Animal Drug Management Act and referred to Yunlin District Prosecutors Office. Officials urge compliance and warn against uncertified veterinary medicines; tips via the 118 hotline.

article.articleHeadline: Punjab logs 451 dengue cases, Ludhiana worst-hit
article.articleSummary: As of September 21, Punjab reported 451 confirmed dengue cases across 21 of 23 districts. Ludhiana leads with 52 cases, followed by Gurdaspur (50), Patiala (38), SAS Nagar (36), Hoshiarpur (33), Kapurthala (29) and Faridkot (28). Other districts report Ferozepur (19), Fatehgarh Sahib (18), Tarn Taran (17), Bathinda (13) and Amritsar (9); Moga 9, Pathankot 8, Fazilka 9; Shri Muktsar Sahib 6; Barnala 4; Mansa and Malerkotla have no confirmed cases so far. Officials caution that private hospitals and laboratories may detect dengue positives not fully captured in district data, as private facilities have been asked to retest samples at government labs before inclusion, a practice some providers reportedly discourage, raising concerns of underreporting during rising transmission.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: MBG Poisoning Case in Kediri, Health Office Says There Is E. coli Bacteria in Food Samples.
article.articleSummary: Escherichia coli contamination linked to a suspected food-poisoning outbreak after MBG (Makan Bergizi Gratis) meals in Kediri City, East Java, Indonesia. Laboratory tests detected E. coli in samples of white rice and melon from MBG servings, associated with 37 students across three elementary schools: SDN Kampung Dalem 3, SDN Kampung Dalem 4, and SDN Kaliombo. The illness followed meals on September 17, 2026; symptoms are not detailed in the report. Authorities did not disclose bacterial load or exact contamination source. The Kediri Health Office (Dinkes) urges heightened vigilance among MBG nutrition service units (SPPG); the Kaliombo kitchen has been suspended, with follow-up actions planned for other kitchens. Officials also call for differentiated menus by student class to reduce risk. The case underscores food safety in school nutrition programs and ongoing investigations, with no information on imported or exported cases.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: [Exclusive] Even amid foot-and-mouth disease outbreak, about 80 livestock farmers head to China... Controversy over 'biosecurity complacency' at Gimpo Livestock Cooperative Association
article.articleSummary: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD), SAT1-type, prompted Korea’s agriculture ministry to warn against travel to outbreak regions and to enforce vaccination and disinfection. In this climate, about 80 livestock industry personnel from Gimpo City’s Livestock Cooperative Association undertook two study trips to China, departing September 12 and 15, visiting Yanji and the Baekdu Mountain area. The second group remained through September 16, when an FMD outbreak occurred in Ganghwa near Seoul; the association’s chairman returned earlier, while others completed the itinerary. Domestic risk followed a September 3 FMD outbreak in Yecheon County, with authorities urging strict biosecurity and travel abstinence to outbreak countries. Critics say the trips reflect complacency, while supporters contend departures occurred before the Ganghwa incident and complied with rules. Contextual figures include 400 Hanwoo cattle in Daegot and vaccination of roughly 13,000 cattle/goats across about 200 Gimpo farms in early September.

article.articleHeadline: 买海鲜混入毒蟹险酿大祸 螃蟹季食鲜小心这些海洋"毒物" _光明网
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Seafood contaminated with poisonous crabs could trigger a major disaster; during crab season, beware these marine "toxins"
article.articleSummary: Published 2026-09-23. Seafood contaminated with poisonous crabs could trigger a major disaster during crab season. A market incident where a small crab mixed with squid was identified as a red-spotted crab carrying tetrodotoxin; even tiny amounts can be fatal, and high-heat cooking does not destroy the toxin. The article lists dangerous marine organisms and regions: red-spotted crab and copper-crusted crab (both with tetrodotoxin) found around Japan, the Philippines, Singapore, and China’s Guangdong and Hainan; textile cone snail and blue-ringed octopus with tetrodotoxin; box jellyfish with severe venom. Spoiled shrimp and crabs can harbor Vibrio parahaemolyticus, reaching pathogenic levels within six hours at 35°C. Prevention tips: avoid unfamiliar seafood, buy from reputable markets, keep raw and cooked seafood separate, and cook to 100°C. Vulnerable groups should avoid raw or undercooked seafood. Three rules: don’t eat unfamiliar, don’t buy unfamiliar, don’t handle unfamiliar seafood.

article.articleHeadline: Bhopal Food Safety Action: खाने से पहले सावधान ! चूहों, कॉकरोच के बीच बन रही 30 की तंदूरी, 600 रुपए वाली सब्जी | Risk Of Food Poisoning From Food At Bhopal Luxury Hotels Has Increased
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Bhopal Food Safety Action: Be careful before eating! A 30-rupee tandoori being prepared among rats and cockroaches, a 600-rupee vegetable dish | Risk Of Food Poisoning From Food At Bhopal Luxury Hotels Has Increased.
article.articleSummary: Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, India — A food-safety report on 3- and 5-star hotels in Bhopal reveals hazardous kitchen conditions. For a 30-rupee tandoori and a 600-rupee vegetable dish, kitchens reportedly house rats and cockroaches on shelves, cutting areas, and cooking zones; staff health certificates and hygiene training are often missing. Mushrooms show fungal growth; onions are spoiled and potatoes rotten; samples are being tested for adulterated paneer. Ranjit Resort on Narmadapuram Road reportedly lacks staff fitness checks. Hotels such as Bhavisha Hotel & Club, Indian Café House MP Nagar, Sayaji, Tortokize, Palash, and Ranjit Lake View were cited; about 80% of large hotels had frying pans that burn black, with 12 notices issued. Gurukrupa Caterers of Bavariya reported cockroaches in the kitchen. Mycotoxins and aflatoxins from moldy produce can cause vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal cramps, and liver damage; cockroaches can spread typhoid and chronic GI infections. Authorities vow action to restore food quality.

article.articleHeadline: India News | India Reaffirms Commitment to Eliminate Hepatitis B, C as Public Health Threats by 2030
article.articleSummary: India reaffirms commitment to eliminate Hepatitis B and C as public health threats by 2030 at UNGA 81 side event 'Advancing Global Action to Eliminate Hepatitis' in New Delhi. Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava outlined a comprehensive, people-centred approach spanning prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment and care, aligned with Sustainable Development Goals. In parallel, CDSCO issued an advisory to curb indiscriminate use of NSAIDs and antibiotics due to Chronic Kidney Disease risk, with DGHS stating these drugs must be used only when clinically indicated under supervision. The Drugs and Cosmetics Act (1940) and its rules regulate import, manufacture, sale and distribution, with NSAIDs primarily in Schedule H and antibiotics in Schedule H1, both requiring warnings and prescription-only sale under Schedule rules. This reflects India’s efforts to strengthen hepatitis control while tightening pharmaceutical governance to mitigate drug-related harms.

article.articleHeadline: IOM Chief Urges Aid Amid DRC's Biggest Ebola Crisis
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak, declared in May 2026, has reached over 7,400 confirmed cases and more than 3,600 deaths as of 16 September, the largest Ebola crisis in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). IOM expands surveillance along major mobility routes, river corridors, and border points to curb cross-border spread, focusing on displacement sites where overcrowding and weak WASH impede access to care. Using population mobility mapping and flow monitoring, IOM targets high-risk corridors and points of entry, including the Congo River route to Kinshasa; at the Bende-Bende PoC, about 1,000 health screenings are conducted daily alongside traveler screening and preparedness activities. IOM reports over 33 million health screenings regionwide and ongoing information and referrals. Neighboring countries—Uganda, South Sudan, Burundi, Rwanda, Central African Republic—are engaged. IOM seeks USD 110 million for a multi-country Ebola Preparedness and Response Plan; USD 29.6 million has been received, with a sizable funding gap. Supported by US Government, CERF, EU, Japan, and World Bank.

article.articleSummary: As of 23 September 2026, Quảng Trị Province’s Center for Disease Control announced laboratory results for a bread-related food poisoning incident in Cam Lộ. Results from Pasteur Institute Nha Trang: 10 of 13 patient samples positive for Salmonella spp; 1/13 positive for Salmonella spp and Staphylococcus aureus. Food samples yielded Salmonella spp in 3/11 samples; Salmonella spp plus Escherichia coli in 4/11; Salmonella spp plus Staphylococcus in 2/11. Salmonella detected in bread, cha bo (beef sausage), cha ca (fish cake), vegetables, braised meat, cucumber, sandwich bread, and water samples. The outbreak prompted hospitalization of 42 people with gastroenteritis after consuming bread at a local establishment; authorities are coordinating investigations, restricting the business, and implementing prevention measures to identify the infection source and prevent further cases.

DF was then brought to a Kalanganyar clinic, where blood examination confirmed dengue fever. The report documents a pediatric dengue case in Lebak with laboratory confirmation.

article.articleSummary: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee Ka-chiu and his team today, 23 September 2026, led by example as the seasonal influenza vaccination program has started and urged residents to vaccinate early to build a community immunity barrier against influenza and its complications. Lee said vaccination is one of the most effective ways to prevent seasonal flu, and can reduce influenza-related hospitalizations and deaths. To encourage uptake, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government announced four optimization measures: (1) refine vaccine procurement to source vaccines from multiple suppliers rather than a single supplier; (2) add electronic consent form functionality on the MediHealth Pass; (3) raise the Physician Vaccination Procurement Pilot program quota to 300,000 doses and broaden the eligible doctor base; (4) deepen mobilization of community efforts. The measures aim to protect individuals and families during the upcoming flu season.

article.articleHeadline: 呼吸道合胞病毒将进入流行季，"一老一小"是高风险人群，抗生素治疗无效
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Respiratory Syncytial Virus to Enter the Epidemic Season; the elderly and the very young are high-risk groups; antibiotic treatment is ineffective.
article.articleSummary: RSV enters its typical peak season (October–April). Beijing You’an Hospital infectious disease expert Li Tongzeng notes there is no specific antiviral; treatment is supportive. Young children, especially under one year, and older adults with COPD, diabetes, or immune compromise are high-risk for pneumonia and potentially respiratory failure. Early RSV symptoms resemble a common cold—nasal congestion, runny nose, mild cough and fever—but RSV can progress to lower respiratory tract infection with higher fever, wheeze, chest tightness, and, in infants, irritability or poor feeding. Most mild cases can be managed at home with rest, fluids, antipyretics, saline nasal irrigation, and humidification; nebulization may relieve symptoms. Severe cases require hospitalization with oxygen and respiratory support. A long-acting monoclonal antibody is approved in China for infants under six months or those with congenital heart disease or chronic lung disease to reduce infection and severe outcomes. Adults have low risk but can transmit to high-risk household members; emphasize ventilation, hand hygiene, and masking in enclosed spaces.

article.articleHeadline: Anak 7 Tahun Positif DBD Disebut Ditolak Puskesmas, Kadinkes Lebak Buka Suara
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 7-Year-Old Child Tests Positive for Dengue Fever, Allegedly Rejected by a Community Health Center, Lebak Health Office Head Speaks Out.
article.articleSummary: As of 23 September 2026, a 7-year-old in Lebak Regency, Banten, tested positive for dengue fever (DBD) after initial care at Puskesmas Warunggunung. Health office head Eka Darmana Putra said the child was not refused treatment; inpatient beds were full, so staff advised outpatient management and return the next morning for laboratory testing, with the morning lab technician on duty. In emergencies, Puskesmas should refer to RSUD. The team will visit the patient’s home for follow-up and to conduct an epidemiological investigation (PE) to confirm whether infection arose from local mosquito bites and to perform fogging if warranted. The family reported being sent home despite fever up to 40°C, delirium, and unresponsiveness; later, after treatment at a clinic in Kalanganyar, the child tested positive for DBD. Public health measures are being considered to curb transmission.

triage.headline_ja: 7歳の子供がデング熱陽性、保健所に診療拒否されたとの報道、レバック県保健局長が説明
triage.triage_reason: インドネシアの風土病であるデング熱の単発症例に関する医療対応（診療拒否疑惑）を扱ったローカルニュースであり、公衆衛生上の異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: デング熱はインドネシアで流行性の風土病であり、本記事は個別患者の医療対応（診療拒否疑惑）に焦点を当てたローカルニュース。地域内の疫学調査（PE）とフォギングは通常の対応であり、シグナルとしての重大性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: IDAI Rekomendasikan 6 Langkah Tangani Influenza A Anak
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: IDAI Recommends 6 Steps to Manage Influenza A in Children
article.articleSummary: Influenza A in Indonesian children is rising, with H3N2 subclade K, nicknamed 'Super Flu', detected in 13 provinces. IDAI reports about 5% of pediatric cases require hospitalization; among those, 80% are under 2 years old and roughly half under 6 months. Severe outcomes include pneumonia, asthma exacerbation, myocarditis, and encephalopathy in at‑risk children. IDAI’s six steps: 1) annual vaccination from 6 months for all children and household members; inactivated (trivalent/quadrivalent) vaccines and intranasal live vaccine for ages 2–49 healthy; reduces infection risk by 40–60%. 2) maintain hygiene: handwashing, masking, distancing, cough etiquette. 3) recognize symptoms and seek prompt care; RT-PCR as needed. 4) keep sick children home; isolate until 24 hours fever‑free without antipyretics. 5) prevent dehydration; ensure fluids; antivirals only after doctor’s evaluation. 6) strengthen genomic surveillance and RT‑PCR access to identify subtypes, including subclade K. Globally, influenza causes about 1 billion infections annually. Collaboration among health workers, government, and communities is urged to protect children.

triage.headline_ja: IDAI、小児インフルエンザA対応の6つのステップを推奨
triage.triage_reason: H3N2 subclade K（通称'Super Flu'）がインドネシア13州の小児に拡大し、重症合併症や入院例が報告されており、新規亜系統による異常な流行拡大とみなされるため。
triage.notes: H3N2 subclade Kは新規亜系統として国際的に注目されており、乳幼児における重症化（肺炎、心筋炎、脳症）が報告されている点で通常の季節性インフルエンザ以上の懸念がある。ただし外部支援の必要性については記事に記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: गढ़वा में लेप्टोस्पायरोसिस की दस्तक! 2 मरीजों की पुष्टि, बरसात में ऐसे फैलता है संक्रमण; स्वास्थ्य विभाग अलर्ट - leptospirosis and scrub typhus alert in garhwa jharkhand
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Leptospirosis knocks in Garhwa, Jharkhand! Two cases confirmed, this is how the infection spreads during the monsoon; Health Department alert.
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis outbreaks in Garhwa district, Jharkhand, with two confirmed cases (Bardag and Kharoondi area) during the monsoon season. The infection is caused by Leptospira bacteria in water/soil contaminated with urine from animals (rats, dogs, goats, cows, buffaloes, horses). Symptoms include high fever, chills, severe headache, back and calf pain, conjunctival redness, jaundice-like appearance, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea; diagnosis is essential due to symptom overlap with dengue, malaria, or typhus. Transmission rises in rain-fed environments with standing water and mud exposure; protective measures include knee-high boots, waterproof bandages for wounds, avoiding contact with contaminated water, and using gloves, masks, and eye protection when handling animals. Testing and treatment are free at local health centers. In Bardag, four other patients have Scrub Typhus; seven total cases discussed. One additional Bardag patient tested in Latehar; results pending, samples sent to RIMS Ranchi.

triage.headline_ja: ジャールカンド州ガルワでレプトスピラ症発生！2例確認、雨季の感染拡大に注意；保健局が警戒
triage.triage_reason: インド・ジャールカンド州の一地域における季節性のレプトスピラ症・つつが虫病の小規模発生で、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低いが、雨季を通じた曝露継続の可能性があるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: レプトスピラ症・つつが虫病はいずれも人畜共通感染症で動物由来。地方保健局が無料検査・治療を提供しており対応中。雨季の間、住民の継続的な曝露リスクがある点でWPRO基準の一部に該当するが、重症度・死亡例などの詳細情報は不明。

article.articleHeadline: बुखार के साथ शरीर पर लाल चकत्ते, कहीं डेंगू तो नहीं? जानें लक्षण
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Fever with red rashes on the body, could it be dengue? Learn the symptoms.
article.articleSummary: Dengue is highlighted as a risk during monsoon-season conditions with fever and body-wide red rashes. WHO guidance notes dengue typically presents with high fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia/joint pain, nausea, vomiting, and rash within 4–10 days after a bite from an infected Aedes mosquito. Most cases are mild and resolve in 1–2 weeks, but some progress to severe dengue. A key warning: fever resolution does not always mean recovery; warning signs around defervescence include severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, nasal or gum bleeding, rapid breathing, marked weakness or restlessness, blood in vomit or stool, and skin that is cold or pale—seek urgent medical care. There is no specific antiviral therapy; treatment is supportive with rest, fluids, and symptom control. Paracetamol can be used for fever/pain; avoid aspirin and ibuprofen. Prevention centers on eliminating standing water, covering water storage, wearing long sleeves, and using repellents, as well as protecting patients to prevent mosquito transmission.

triage.headline_ja: 発熱と体の赤い発疹、それはデング熱かも？症状を知る
triage.triage_reason: 特定の発生事例やアウトブレイクの報告ではなく、デング熱の症状・予防に関する一般的な健康啓発記事であるため、シグナルとしての基準に該当しない。
triage.notes: 記事は特定の国・地域での発生報告ではなく、デング熱の症状・治療・予防に関する一般的な健康情報コンテンツ。具体的な症例数や発生地の言及がないため、インドを含め対象国は検証対象外とした。

article.articleHeadline: Dinkes Garut Temukan 7.582 Kasus Positif TB, 81 Meninggal
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Garut Health Office Finds 7,582 Positive TB Cases, 81 Deaths.
article.articleSummary: Garut Regency Health Office, West Java, reports 7,582 residents suspected of tuberculosis (TB) from January through September 2026, including 51 multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) cases and 81 deaths. TB is a bacterial lung infection spread via coughing or sneezing; MDR-TB presents with similar symptoms. Health official Asep Surahman notes a significant uptick, with 51 MDR-TB patients already treated with isoniazid and rifampicin. The district health department is expanding screening and outreach to curb transmission. MDR-TB symptoms include fever, coughing blood, chest pain, night sweats, appetite loss, weight loss, chills, and shortness of breath. Authorities are increasing cross-sector screening and door-to-door outreach, and urge the public to maintain hygiene, avoid contact with TB patients, eat a balanced diet, exercise, and undergo periodic health checks.

triage.headline_ja: ガルット県保健局、結核陽性7,582例発見、81人死亡
triage.triage_reason: 結核はインドネシアにおける既知の風土病であり、地方保健局による定期的な症例報告であって、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 結核（TB）はインドネシアにおいて長年の風土病であり、本記事は地方保健局による年間の症例集計・啓発活動の報告に過ぎない。MDR-TBの51例は懸念材料だが、既存の治療プログラム内で対応されており、新規アウトブレイクや国際的な公衆衛生事象としての特徴は見られない。

article.articleHeadline: 451 dengue, 16 chikungunya cases reported in Punjab - The Tribune
article.articleSummary: Punjab reports 451 dengue and 16 chikungunya cases in 2026, with no confirmed dengue deaths. Through Sept 21, 100,414 dengue samples were tested (64,049 at Aam Aadmi Clinics), yielding a 0.45% positivity. Higher caseloads are in Ludhiana, Kapurthala, Faridkot and Tarn Taran, prompting intensified surveillance and vector-control measures. Health authorities plan aggressive larval source reduction, field surveillance, and door-to-door surveys by ASHA workers and nursing students to locate and eliminate breeding sites; VHSNC meetings will be boosted and there will be incentives for ASHAs. Special directions include indoor and outdoor fogging in priority districts. The minister also reviewed 16 chikungunya cases and broader water-borne diseases, with emphasis on drinking-water quality, leak repairs, and stockpiling ORS, IV fluids, and chlorine tablets. Distribution of Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojana cards was reviewed; residents urged to prevent mosquito breeding.

triage.headline_ja: パンジャブ州でデング熱451例、チクングニヤ16例を報告
triage.triage_reason: インド・パンジャブ州における季節性のデング熱・チクングニヤ発生report。死亡例なく陽性率も低いが、複数地区での発生継続とベクター対策の必要性からWATCH対象とする。
triage.notes: インドでは毎年季節性にデング熱・チクングニヤが発生しており、本件も例年の流行報告に近い。死亡例なし、陽性率0.45%と低く、地方当局が通常の対策（防疫・サーベイランス強化）を実施中で管理可能な状況。国際的拡大リスクや渡航制限の兆候はなし。

article.articleHeadline: Influenza A Meningkat, Anak Berisiko Kena Komplikasi Berat
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Influenza A on the Rise, Children at Risk of Severe Complications.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A, H3N2 subclade nicknamed 'Super Flu', is detected in 13 Indonesian provinces, signaling rising cases in Indonesia. In at‑risk children, influenza can cause pneumonia, asthma exacerbation, myocarditis, and encephalopathy. RT‑PCR is emphasized for lab confirmation to identify the subtype. Globally, influenza causes about 1 billion infections annually, with 3–5 million severe cases and 290,000–650,000 respiratory deaths. In Indonesia, sentinel surveillance shows year‑round fluctuations with a peak in late 2025 and a resurgence mid‑2026. About 5% of infected children require hospitalization; 80% of these are under 2 years, and 50% under 6 months. Transmission can occur from 24 hours before symptoms to 10 days after; isolation at home is advised. Prevention includes non‑pharmacologic measures and annual vaccination from 6 months; vaccines are inactivated (trivalent/quadrivalent) and intranasal live (2–49 healthy), reducing infection by 40–60% and disease severity. Vaccination is yearly due to drift/shift.

triage.headline_ja: インフルエンザAが増加、子供は重篤な合併症のリスクあり
triage.triage_reason: インドネシア13州でH3N2サブクレード（通称『Super Flu』）による季節性インフルエンザ増加が報告されているが、通常の季節性流行の範囲内とも考えられ、異常性や国際的拡大リスクの明確な情報は不足している。子供の重症化リスクへの言及があるため継続的な注視が必要。
triage.notes: H3N2サブクレード『Super Flu』というニックネームが注目を集めているが、記事内容は季節性インフルエンザサーベイランスに基づく一般的な健康啓発情報であり、新規変異株としての異常性やパンデミック化リスクについての明確な記述はない。続報でサブクレードの特性や重症度データを確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: டெங்கு தடுப்பு நடவடிக்கைகள் தீவிரம்; மக்கள் வசிக்கும் இடத்தில் மருத்துவ பரிசோதனை!
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue prevention measures intensified; medical testing in residential areas!
article.articleSummary: Ranipet district in Tamil Nadu intensifies dengue and other fever prevention. In Walajapet Municipality and surrounding rural areas, the health department has intensified measures, running about 60 fever-detection medical camps daily for public welfare. Through these camps, tests for dengue and other fevers are conducted; daily blood samples from roughly 100–140 individuals are collected and sent for laboratory analysis. Vector-control activities include cleaning drains, collecting and disposing household garbage, and timely removal of standing water after rains; breeding sites for mosquitoes are targeted. Medical teams monitor public health by conducting examinations for fevers and related health issues, with blood samples tested to identify causes. Public cooperation is essential: ensure no standing water, proper garbage disposal; seek immediate care at government hospitals or medical camps if fever symptoms occur.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱予防対策を強化;住宅地域での医療検診を実施!
triage.triage_reason: インド・タミルナードゥ州で通常のデング熱予防活動が報じられているが、異常な流行拡大や重症例急増を示す情報はなく、行政の定型的な予防・監視活動の一環と考えられる。
triage.notes: デング熱は毎年インドで季節的に発生する疾患であり、本記事は地方自治体による予防的な医療キャンプ・ベクターコントロール活動の報告にとどまる。症例数や死亡者数の急増を示すデータはない。

article.articleHeadline: 6 Cara Sederhana Mencegah Penularan Influenza A
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 6 Simple Ways to Prevent the Transmission of Influenza A.
article.articleSummary: As of 23 September 2026, Indonesia reports an uptick in influenza A(H1N1) cases, though officials urge not to overreact while mitigation is prepared. The circulating virus is a genetically evolved descendant of the 2009 pandemic H1N1 strain. Public health expert Professor Tri Wibawa of Gadjah Mada University notes influenza commonly involves types A and B, with symptoms including fever or chills, cough, sore throat, runny nose or congestion, muscle/body aches, headache, and fatigue. High-risk groups for complications include those over 65, children under five, people with chronic diseases, and the immunocompromised. To reduce transmission, several simple preventive steps are advised. Reporting from Liputan6.com in Jakarta.

triage.headline_ja: インフルエンザA型感染を防ぐ6つの簡単な方法
triage.triage_reason: インドネシアでインフルエンザA(H1N1)症例の増加が報告され、2009年パンデミック株の遺伝的変異株とされているが、当局は過剰反応を控えるよう呼びかけており重症度や拡大の詳細情報が不足しているため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 記事は予防啓発が主目的であり、症例数・重症度・地理的拡大等の具体的データは記載されていない。遺伝的に進化したH1N1株の増加という表現はあるが、当局は『過剰反応しないように』と述べており、現時点でのリスクは低いとみられる。続報で症例数や重症度の詳細が確認され次第、再評価が必要。

diseases.name: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1

article.articleHeadline: Pakar UGM Ungkap Gejala-Cara Cegah Influenza A yang Kasusnya Lagi 'Ngegas' di RI
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: UGM expert reveals symptoms and ways to prevent Influenza A, whose cases are surging again in Indonesia
article.articleSummary: Influenza A cases are surging in Indonesia. Ministry of Health data through September 12, 2026 show influenza positivity at 38% in week 35, up from 22% the prior week. Of 175 specimens tested, 66 were positive, with most identified as influenza A(H1N1)pdm09. UGM microbiology professor Tri Wibawa notes the rise should not cause undue panic, but warrants risk mitigation. Typical symptoms include fever (sometimes with chills), cough, sore throat, runny or congested nose, muscle/body aches, headache, and fatigue. High-risk groups are older adults (≥65), children under 5, people with chronic diseases, and those with weakened immune systems. Prevention emphasizes healthy living, hand hygiene, proper cough/sneeze etiquette, mask use when ill, and vaccination, especially for high-risk individuals. The circulating A(H1N1) strain is a descendant of the 2009 pandemic H1N1 virus with genetic changes.

triage.headline_ja: UGM専門家がインフルエンザAの症状と予防法を解説、インドネシアで感染例が再び増加
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザA(H1N1)pdm09の陽性率上昇に関する一般向け健康情報記事であり、専門家自身が『過度な心配は不要』と明言している。既知の株で異常性・国際的拡大リスクは認められず、社会的関心も一般的な健康啓発レベルに留まる。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザA(H1N1)pdm09（2009年パンデミック株の子孫）の陽性率上昇に関する報道。専門家はパニック不要と述べ、通常の予防策（衛生管理、ワクチン接種）を推奨するのみで、重症例や集団感染の具体的報告はない。

locations.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

article.articleHeadline: David Miliband: Trump to blame for Ebola outbreak that killed thousands
article.articleSummary: DR Congo faces an Ebola outbreak that has claimed more than 3,000 lives since May, according to David Miliband, head of the International Rescue Committee. He attributes the resurgence to funding cuts by the Trump administration and to successive reductions in international development aid, arguing that even a fraction of aid can save lives. Miliband stresses there is now clearer evidence of what works, including randomized controlled trials showing impact. In DR Congo, he says U.S. funding cuts left hospitals and communities without essential infection prevention and control, washing facilities, and latrines, enabling transmission. He contends the Treasury dictates UK aid levels, limiting the Foreign Secretary's ability to respond. Miliband uses the outbreak to illustrate broader consequences of aid withdrawal, while praising incoming UK PM's urgency and focus in tackling social challenges.

triage.headline_ja: デイビッド・ミリバンド：数千人の死者を出したエボラ流行はトランプ氏の責任
triage.triage_reason: DRCで3000人以上が死亡したエボラ流行が継続中との報道であり、深刻な公衆衛生影響と資金不足による感染拡大リスクが示唆されているため、フルRRAへの移行が妥当。
triage.notes: 記事は主に国際援助資金削減の政治的批判が主題だが、DRCにおけるエボラ流行の深刻さ（3000人以上死亡、感染対策インフラの欠如）を示す一次情報を含む。米国・英国は発生地域ではなく政治的議論の文脈のため verified_locations から除外。続報にて感染者数・国際的封じ込め状況の確認が必要。

locations.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

article.articleHeadline: David Miliband: Trump to blame for Ebola outbreak that has killed thousands
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed more than 3,000 people since May, Miliband says, blaming cuts in overseas aid for weakening the response. As president and CEO of the International Rescue Committee, he notes U.S. funding cuts left Ebola prevention and outbreak control under-resourced, with poor washing facilities and latrines. He cites that the IRC’s budget fell from $1.5 billion to $1 billion under the Trump administration. Miliband also criticizes UK aid reductions, from 0.5% to 0.3% of national income, arguing that even a fraction of aid saves lives: about 45 million children acutely malnourished, 14 million women with life-threatening episodes in childbirth, and roughly 2 million deaths from bleeding. He stresses that the Treasury ultimately dictates aid spending, not the foreign secretary, and urges sustained investment to prevent further outbreaks.

triage.headline_ja: デイビッド・ミリバンド：数千人を死亡させたエボラ流行の責任はトランプにある
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおけるエボラ流行で3000人以上の死亡が報じられており、援助削減による対応力低下も指摘されているため、公衆衛生上深刻かつ管理可能性に懸念があるシグナルとして識別。
triage.notes: 本記事は政治的論評（援助削減批判）が主目的であり、疫学的詳細（発生地域内訳、感染者数の内訳、WHO公式発表との整合性）が不明。3000人超という死亡数はDRCの近年のエボラ流行規模と比べ非常に大きく、数値の正確性について公式情報源での確認が必要。米国・英国は援助国として言及されているのみで発生国ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: NCDC introduces new measures for travellers into Nigeria
article.articleSummary: Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) measures announced by Nigeria’s NCDC in response to the ongoing outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Travellers from countries with active or relevant EVD transmission may be required to complete Health Declaration Forms to support surveillance, risk assessment, contact follow-up, and early detection; travellers from other countries are temporarily exempt, reflecting a risk-based approach. The advisory follows consultations with public health experts and the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, aiming to keep Nigeria's preparedness proportionate to identified risks. The public is urged to stay vigilant for Ebola symptoms and seek medical attention if exposed or symptomatic; individuals with travel or exposure history should provide accurate information to healthcare workers. Preparatory activities are ongoing and measures will be updated as epidemiological information evolves, with coordination among the Federal Ministry of Health, Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, Port Health Services, NIS, and NCAA, and support from WHO and Africa CDC.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ:NCDC(ナイジェリア疾病予防管理センター)がナイジェリア入国者向けの新たな対策を導入
triage.triage_reason: DRCで進行中のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクに対し、ナイジェリアが渡航者への健康申告制度を含む水際対策を導入したもので、IHR基準の複数項目（深刻性・国際拡大リスク・渡航制限）に該当するためフルRRAでの評価が妥当。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はナイジェリアにおける渡航者対策の導入だが、その発端はDRCで継続中のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクであるため、実際の感染症発生国としてDRCをverified_locationsに含めた。ナイジェリア自体は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。WHO・Africa CDCとの連携が言及されており国際的関心の高さがうかがえる。

article.articleHeadline: नोएडा : मौसम में बदलाव के साथ बढ़ा डेंगू का प्रकोप, 12 दिन में 85 मरीज मिले, अस्पतालों में अलर्ट जारी
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Noida: Dengue outbreak intensifies with change in weather; 85 patients diagnosed in 12 days; hospitals on alert.
article.articleSummary: Noida reports a dengue outbreak intensifying with weather changes. Over the past 12 days, 85 dengue cases have been diagnosed in the district, with six new confirmations in the last 24 hours. Health officials note an average of about seven new cases daily over nearly two weeks, prompting hospitals to remain on high alert. The Aedes mosquito-borne disease thrives amid fluctuating temperatures, so authorities urge residents to eliminate standing water in homes, societies, and surrounding areas. Regular checks of coolers, flower pots, old tires, rooftops, and other potential water-holding spots are advised. Symptoms to watch include fever, severe headache, body and joint pains, behind-the-eye pain, and extreme weakness; seek medical advice and avoid self-medication. The health department is intensifying vector-control activities and public-awareness campaigns to curb transmission; no deaths are reported in the article.

triage.headline_ja: ノイダ：気候変動でデング熱の流行が拡大、12日間で85人の患者が発見、病院に警戒指令
triage.triage_reason: 季節性のデング熱流行で死者報告はなく、規模も局地的だが、症例増加傾向がありベクター対策の継続が必要なため経過観察とする。

article.articleHeadline: Rubella Virus : चेहऱ्यावरील लाल पुरळ अन् ताप दुर्लक्ष करू नका; डॉक्टरांकडून सावधगिरी बाळगण्याचे आवाहन
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rubella Virus: Do not ignore red rashes on the face and fever; doctors urge caution.
article.articleSummary: Rubella cases in Jharkhand’s Simdega district have spurred intensified oversight and vaccination in the Thethaitangar block. On 22 September, a blood sample from a 10-year-old girl in Mundatoli tested positive for rubella, though a subsequent report that day denied it; by 23 September, a second boy in the Taraboga area of Thethaitangar was confirmed with rubella. Health teams are conducting house-to-house screening and targeting children who have not received the second MR dose; 112 children were identified as eligible, with 28 vaccinated since 20 September. Special vaccination camps are being organized. Rubella spreads via respiratory droplets and causes a facial rash that can spread to the body; it is particularly dangerous for pregnant women (Congenital Rubella Syndrome). One MR dose offers about 97% protection. Jharkhand also reported 17 measles outbreaks Jan–Aug, prompting a Measles-Rubella War Room.

triage.headline_ja: ルビラウイルス：顔の赤い発疹と発熱を軽視しないで；医師が注意喚起
triage.triage_reason: インド・ジャールカンド州の一地区で数例の風疹症例確認とワクチン接種活動が進行中だが、重症例や広域拡大の報告はなく、国際的な公衆衛生上の緊急性は低いため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 地区レベルでの風疹（および麻疹）の小規模流行に対し、地元保健当局が家庭訪問スクリーニングとMRワクチン接種キャンペーンを実施中。確定症例数は少数（2例）で、重症・死亡例の報告なし。国際的拡大や渡航制限の懸念は現時点で認められない。

article.articleHeadline: "الصحة العالمية": "إيبولا" لا يزال خارج السيطرة في الكونغو
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: "World Health Organization": "Ebola" remains out of control in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains out of control, according to the World Health Organization, despite a slight decline in cases. As of Sunday, there have been 7,733 confirmed cases and 3,732 deaths across 63 health zones in seven provinces. Declared in May, this is the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in DRC history and the second-largest globally after West Africa’s 2014–2016 outbreak. The expansion includes the Dungu health zone in Haut-Uele Province, adjacent to South Sudan, increasing cross-border transmission risk. Geographic spread is widening, straining response resources. About two-thirds of recent deaths occurred outside health facilities, suggesting delayed detection and limited access to care. Domestic risk is assessed as very high, with regional risk high, underscoring ongoing surveillance, outbreak control, and health-system challenges in the country."} ,

triage.headline_ja: 「世界保健機関」：エボラ出血熱はコンゴ民主共和国で依然として制御不能
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国史上最大・最悪のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクであり、国境を越えた感染拡大リスク（南スーダンへの拡大）も指摘されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: 記事にはSouth Sudanとの国境地域（Haut-Uele州のDungu保健区）への拡大も言及されているが、South Sudanは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCが主題であり対象国リストに含まれるため記載。

article.articleHeadline: नोएडा : मौसम में बदलाव के साथ बढ़ा डेंगू का प्रकोप, 12 दिन में 85 मरीज मिले, अस्पतालों में अलर्ट जारी - Punjab Kesari
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Noida: Dengue fever outbreak surges with change in weather; 85 patients reported in 12 days; hospitals on alert - Punjab Kesari
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever outbreak intensifies in Noida, India as weather fluctuations sustain transmission. In the last 12 days, dengue infections have risen to 85, with six new cases confirmed in the past 24 hours. Health authorities have heightened surveillance and issued alerts to hospitals and health centers to remain vigilant. The Aedes mosquito, thriving in standing water around homes, is the primary vector. Authorities urge residents to eliminate water accumulation in homes, societies, and surroundings, regularly inspect coolers, flower pots, old tires, rooftops, and other places where water can collect. Typical dengue symptoms include fever, severe headache, body and joint pains, retro-orbital pain, and marked weakness. People are advised to seek medical care promptly and avoid self-medication. Officials are accelerating vector-control activities and awareness campaigns to curb transmission.

triage.headline_ja: ノイダ:気候変動に伴いデング熱が拡大、12日間で85人の患者確認、病院に警戒指令

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Noida: Dengue fever outbreak intensifies with changing weather; 85 patients in 12 days, hospitals on alert.
article.articleSummary: As of 23 September 2026, Noida is witnessing a dengue fever outbreak intensifying with seasonal weather changes. The health department reports 85 dengue cases confirmed in the past 12 days, with six new infections confirmed in the last 24 hours. On average, about seven new dengue patients have been reported daily over the preceding two weeks, prompting hospitals to remain on alert. Authorities urge clinics to maintain vigilance, with rapid testing and treatment for suspected cases. The primary vector is Aedes mosquitoes that breed in stagnant water around homes and neighborhoods; residents are advised to eliminate standing water in households, societies, and nearby areas. Regular checks of coolers, planters, old tires, rooftops, and other water-holding sites are recommended. Symptoms to seek care include fever, severe headache, body and joint pains, pain behind the eyes, or marked weakness; self-medication is discouraged. Public awareness and vector-control activities are intensified to curb transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Menu MBG yang Picu Keracunan Ratusan Siswa di Pati Positif Sejumlah Bakteri |Republika Online
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: MBG Menu That Triggered Food Poisoning Among Hundreds of Students in Pati, Positive for Several Bacteria
article.articleSummary: An outbreak of foodborne illness linked to MBG free nutritious meals sickened hundreds of students at MTsN 3 Pati and SMPN 1 Gembong in Pati Regency, Central Java, Indonesia, with additional cases at MTs Manbaul Ulum in Gembong where a dozen or so students were affected. The meals were served on Sept 8, 2026; authorities declared it an extraordinary event. Laboratory tests on five food samples found two positives: fried rice contained Escherichia coli, Bacillus species, and Bacillus cereus; tempeh contained Bacillus species and Bacillus cereus. Other tested items (cucumber, watermelon, crackers) were negative. Vomitus samples were positive for Bacillus species and Bacillus cereus; stools positive for E. coli and Staphylococcus aureus. E. coli likely from contaminated water; Bacillus from intestinal sources; Staph from food handlers’ hands. Recommendations target SPGP-equipped units to improve sanitation and provide filtered clean water. MBG was supplied by SPPG 1 Gembong.

triage.headline_ja: パティ県で数百人の生徒に食中毒を引き起こしたMBG給食メニュー、複数の細菌が陽性
triage.triage_reason: 単一施設（学校）での給食を原因とする集団食中毒事例であり、ヒト-ヒト感染や国際的拡大の可能性は低く、国内の食品安全管理上の問題として対応可能なため。
triage.notes: 食品由来の汚染（E. coli、Bacillus cereus、Staphylococcus aureus）による学校給食での集団食中毒。感染性疾患のヒト-ヒト伝播ではなく、食品衛生管理の問題。地域当局は既に調査・対応中であり、国際的な公衆衛生リスクは認められない。

article.articleHeadline: Wali Kota Bandung Ungkap IGD Rumah Sakit Dipenuhi Pasien Flu dan Demam Tinggi, Influenza A? |Republika Online
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Bandung Mayor Reveals Hospital Emergency Department Filled with Patients with Flu and High Fever, Influenza A? | Republika Online
article.articleSummary: Bandung Mayor Muhammad Farhan reported that the city’s emergency departments (ER/IGD) are crowded with patients presenting flu-like illness and high fever, including cough and runny nose. Hospitals assure continued access to care and do not turn patients away, with some private facilities busier than usual. Swab samples from flu patients at community health centers (puskesmas) will be sent to the Ministry of Health for testing to determine whether it is Influenza A. City authorities say Bandung is managing the situation and will treat severe flu cases promptly. He urged masks for travelers on public transport and advised students with flu to refrain from attending school, noting masks for schoolchildren are optional. No case counts were provided, but facilities and healthcare workers are described as prepared and under control.

triage.headline_ja: バンドン市長、病院ERがインフルエンザ様症状・高熱の患者で混雑していると発表、Influenza A疑い｜Republika Online

article.articleHeadline: Pemkot Bengkulu gencarkan skrining antisipasi penyebaran TBC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Bengkulu City Government steps up TB screening to prevent its spread.
article.articleSummary: Bengkulu City Government in Bengkulu Province, Indonesia, has intensified tuberculosis (TB) screening to curb spread. From January to September 2026, 864 residents were infected with TB, while screening efforts, including the free health check program (CKG) alongside TB screening, have yielded 824 suspected TB cases this year. City Health Office head Nelli Hartati says expanded screening and partnerships with puskesmas (community health centers) and health foundations aim to detect new cases early and reduce transmission, moving toward the goal of zero TB cases by 2035. Residents are urged to seek testing if coughing for more than two weeks, with sputum analysis at puskesmas or other health facilities. The initiative emphasizes rapid case finding and public education on TB transmission and the importance of completing treatment, addressing adherence challenges due to lengthy therapy.

article.articleHeadline: Vĩnh Long ghi nhận nhiều trường hợp tử vong do bệnh dại
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Vĩnh Long reports numerous deaths due to rabies.
article.articleSummary: Rabies in Vĩnh Long Province, Vietnam, as of 23 September 2026: 2022–2025 recorded 24 deaths, with no fatalities in 2025. Human post-exposure prophylaxis coverage reached ~100,000 vaccinees annually. Animal health efforts include routine vaccination of pets and event- and vaccination-site–based surveillance; four animal rabies outbreaks were detected in Phước Mỹ Trung, Lộc Thuận, Đồng Khởi, and Thạnh Phước, all identified through surveillance systems. In the first nine months of 2026, six human rabies deaths occurred in Tân Xuân, Hiệp Mỹ, Châu Hưng, Bến Tre, Ba Tri, and Tân Thủy; four animal outbreaks were also recorded. Over 600 warning signs were shared via Zalo to aid rapid veterinary verification; 20 samples were reviewed, with four dog samples testing positive. Authorities will strengthen surveillance, dog/cat population control, animal vaccination, and ensure timely post-exposure prophylaxis for exposed individuals.

article.articleHeadline: Aurora dengue cases surge 137% to 2,172
article.articleSummary: As of 23 September 2026, Aurora province in Central Luzon, Philippines reports dengue cases rising 137% to 2,172. In the latest surveillance week (6–12 Sept), 106 new infections were recorded. Patients ranged from 1 month to 104 years, median 12; children aged 1–10 accounted for 917 cases (42%), with males about half. Cumulative infections are led by Maria Aurora (463), followed by Dilasag (413) and Dingalan (394). Among new cases, San Luis reported 32, Maria Aurora 26, and Dilasag 21. Baler added 11 new infections (total 242); Casiguran 8 (total 253). Dipaculao and Dinalungan each reported 1 new case (totals 69 and 37). Dilasag has the highest attack rate at 23.2 per 1,000. Dengue clusters span 61 barangays; transmission is not confined to a single municipality. Nationwide, 155,918 cases (−33% YoY), Central Luzon highest region with 21,242. Health measures urge elimination of breeding sites, nets, repellents, prompt medical consultation, and targeted fogging where needed; early detection remains critical as rains continue.

article.articleHeadline: ಹುಡಗಿಯ ಕರಿಬಸವೇಶ್ವರ ಶಾಲೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ರೇಬೀಸ್ ಅರಿವು ಶಿಬಿರ - Sanjevani
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rabies Awareness Camp at Hudagi Karibasaveshvara School - Sanjevani
article.articleSummary: Rabies awareness camp organized by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services at Hudgi Karibasaveshvara Higher Primary School in Hudgi, Karnataka. Dr. Shantkumar Siddeshwar, Chief Veterinary Officer, lectured on rabies as a deadly zoonotic disease transmitted to humans and other animals through bites from infected animals. He highlighted clinical signs, the importance of vaccination, and preventive measures for humans, pets, and livestock. World Rabies Day is observed annually on September 28 to honor scientist Louis Pasteur. Karabasappa Valododdi, a senior member of the teaching staff, urged universal cooperation to eradicate rabies. Teachers and students, including Mallikarjun Kunnur, Roopa, Mangala, Sangeetha Hallikhed, Aruna, Pankaja, Nagamani and Renuka, participated, with an on-site quiz awarding prizes to top students.

article.articleHeadline: जिले में छह और पशुओं में लंपी संक्रमण
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Lumpy skin disease infection in six more animals in the district.
article.articleSummary: As of 23 September 2026, Lumpy Skin Disease has been confirmed in six more cattle in the Haldwani district, raising the total infected animals to nine from 42 tested samples; ten samples are awaiting results. Samples were collected from cattle in the Ghodanala, Bindukhatta, Kishanpur, Sakuliya, and Halduchowd areas. The Department of Animal Husbandry is monitoring the affected livestock and informing farmers in the affected zones. Chief Veterinary Officer Dr. Rajiv Singh confirmed laboratory-confirmed Lumpy Skin Disease cases and reported ongoing surveillance and treatment of the infected animals in the district.

article.articleHeadline: Fake Drug Racket Busted In Delhi; 481 Units Of Counterfeit Rabies Vaccine Seized
article.articleSummary: Delhi's Drugs Control Department busted a major fake drug racket in Bhagirath Palace, seizing 481 counterfeit units of Human IP Rabies Vaccine (Purified Vero Cell Rabies Vaccine, Abhayrab) worth about Rs 2 lakh. After a tip‑off, raids on three premises confirmed the batch was not issued by the original manufacturer, M/S Human Biological Institute, Telangana; samples have been sent to the CRI Centre in Kasauli for quality testing. 120 vials were retained as samples; 361 were seized along with seven purchase invoices under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 (Sections 22(1)(C) and 22(1)(CC)). The network traces to an agency in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh; UP authorities raided two Kanpur locations and the agency admitted supplying Delhi. Delhi and UP are jointly investigating to identify the kingpin and distribution chain. Health Minister Dr Pankaj Kumar Singh pledged zero tolerance and strict action.

article.articleHeadline: खूनी दस्त की वजह बन सकती है Bacillary Dysentery बैक्टीरियल बीमारी, क्लीवलैंड क्लिनिक से जानिए लक्षण | Bacillary Dysentery Bloody Diarrhea Symptoms
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Bacillary Dysentery, a Bacterial Disease, Can Cause Bloody Diarrhea; Learn the Symptoms from Cleveland Clinic | Bacillary Dysentery Bloody Diarrhea Symptoms
article.articleSummary: Bacillary dysentery, commonly called Shigellosis, is a bacterial infection of the large intestine caused by Shigella, causing inflammation and ulcers that yield bloody, mucus-laden stools, cramps, fever, and dehydration. Cleveland Clinic notes it spreads rapidly, person-to-person, via poor sanitation, contaminated water or food, and unwashed hands; symptoms typically appear 1–3 days after exposure. Key signs include bloody diarrhea, severe abdominal cramps, fever, tenesmus, nausea, vomiting, and weakness. Diagnosis relies on stool testing to identify Shigella and guide antibiotics; antibiotics are often needed in severe cases. Do not use anti-diarrheal medicines, which can worsen infection. Management emphasizes rehydration with ORS, coconut water, and clear fluids, plus light foods (khichdi, porridge, banana, yogurt). Prevention focuses on handwashing, safe water, cooked foods, and washing produce. Seek care if blood in stool, fever above 101°F, or persistent dehydration. Hong Kong Health Department context is cited for transmission.

triage.headline_ja: 細菌性赤痢(Bacillary Dysentery)は血便を引き起こす細菌性疾患、クリーブランドクリニックが症状を解説
