article.articleHeadline: 'Super Flu' Terdeteksi di 13 Provinsi, Kelompok Ini Paling Rentan Terinfeksi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 'Super Flu' Detected in 13 Provinces, This Group Most at Risk of Infection.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A(H3N2) subclade K, nicknamed 'Super Flu,' has been detected in 13 Indonesian provinces. From January 2026 through 19 September 2026 (Week 37), the majority of cases are in East Java and South Kalimantan, per the Influenza and COVID-19 Case Surveillance Report. Aji Muhawarman of the Ministry of Health notes the data are cumulative for 2026. High-risk groups include young children and the elderly, as well as individuals with comorbidities such as heart disease, cancer, HIV, or those on immunosuppressants or with autoimmune conditions. IDAI expert Nastiti Kaswandani states that influenza A, including H3N2 and subclade K, can cause more severe disease in these groups. Immunization can still reduce transmission and severity; there is no evidence Subclade K is immune to vaccination. Surveillance data through Week 37 of 2026 support ongoing monitoring.

triage.headline_ja: 『スーパーフル』が13州で検出、最も感染リスクが高いグループとは
triage.triage_reason: 新型インフルエンザA(H3N2) subclade K『スーパーフル』がインドネシア13州で検出され、メディア・保健省の注目を集めており、WPRO基準（異常性・流行しやすさ・継続曝露）に複数該当するためフルRRAでの精査が望ましい。
triage.notes: H3N2 subclade Kは新型サブクレードとしてメディアで『Super Flu』と呼称され話題になっているが、実際の重症度や致死率、国際的拡大状況についてのデータは記事中に不明。ワクチンの有効性は維持されているとされる。続報での重症度データ・地理的拡大状況の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Kasus ISPA dan Influenza di Jember Melonjak, Balita Paling Rentan
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cases of Acute Respiratory Infection (ARI) and Influenza in Jember Surged, Toddlers Most Vulnerable
article.articleSummary: Acute Respiratory Infection (ARI) and influenza surged in Jember Regency, East Java, Indonesia, with 348 ARI and 21 influenza cases reported over a four-week period through mid-September 2026. The rise was steepest in the last two weeks. While ARI and influenza affect all ages, toddlers are the most affected group. Transmission occurs primarily via droplets from sneezing or coughing in public spaces, driven by high mobility. Authorities are responding with intensified PHBS (Clean and Healthy Living Behavior) campaigns and strengthening medical services at Puskesmas and hospitals. A digital real-time reporting system tracks daily case dynamics to enable rapid action. Citizens are advised to practice cough etiquette, wear masks when unwell, and wash hands regularly to prevent further spread, amid ongoing community transmission in Jember.

triage.headline_ja: ジェンバーでARI・インフルエンザ症例が急増、幼児が最も脆弱
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザ・ARIの地域的増加であり、当局が通常の公衆衛生対応（啓発活動、医療体制強化）を実施中。IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに該当せず、国際的な懸念や異常性も認められない。
triage.notes: 地域レベル（ジェンバー県）の季節性感染症増加であり、死亡例や重症化の報告はない。地元当局が独自に対応中で外部支援の必要性は示唆されていない。

article.articleHeadline: DOH: Leptospirosis cases up 38% in 2026
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis cases in the Philippines surged in 2026, with 10,936 suspected infections recorded as of Sept 16, up 38% from 7,931 in the same period in 2025. Counts rose from 1,762 (Aug 6–19) to 3,805 (Aug 20–Sept 2). The DOH notes cases in the past 3–4 weeks were 116% higher than the previous 5–6 weeks, pushing nationwide figures past the epidemic threshold. The National Capital Region, Cagayan Valley, and Calabarzon reported the most cases. Of the total, 8,640 cases (79%) were working-age males, median age 33, linked to floodwater exposure amid continuous rains. Doxycycline buffer stocks total 3,727,359 capsules as of Sept 21, replenished across CHDs and national warehouse. DOH is strengthening patient navigation and referrals for timely admission; seek medical care after flood exposure, with or without symptoms.

triage.headline_ja: DOH: レプトスピラ症症例、2026年に38%増加
triage.triage_reason: フィリピンでレプトスピラ症症例が急増し全国的に流行閾値を超えたが、原因は例年の豪雨・洪水暴露によるもので国際的拡大リスクは低く、国内での医薬品供給・対応も進んでいるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 季節性・環境曝露（洪水）による国内アウトブレイクで、DOHがドキシサイクリン備蓄を確保し対応中。人-人感染ではなく国際的拡大リスクは低いが、症例増加傾向が続くため今後の推移を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Cara Cegah Kena Influenza A, Kini Makin Marak Penularannya
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: How to Prevent Contracting Influenza A as Its Spread Becomes More Widespread.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A cases are rising in Indonesia, with data through 12 September 2026 showing 38% lab-positive in week 35; of 175 specimens, 66 were positive, majority influenza A(H1N1)pdm09. Transmission via droplets and contaminated surfaces; higher risk in crowded settings such as offices, schools, and public transport. High-risk groups: adults over 65, children under 5, those with chronic diseases, and immunocompromised. Six prevention steps: 1) healthy lifestyle; 2) cough etiquette; 3) frequent handwashing; 4) avoid close contact with the sick; 5) wear a mask when ill; 6) consider vaccination for at-risk groups. Most cases resolve at home; seek medical care for breathing difficulty, fever >3 days, worsening after improvement, or neurological signs like agitation or seizures. In children, rapid breathing, blue skin, or drowsiness require attention. Reported by Bisnis.com, Jakarta; data from Kemenkes RI and UGM.

triage.headline_ja: インフルエンザA型の感染防止法、感染がますます拡大中
triage.triage_reason: インドネシアでインフルエンザA(H1N1)pdm09の陽性率上昇が報告されているが、季節性インフルエンザの範疇であり、重症例急増や異常な広がりを示す明確な情報はなく、続報を注視するレベル。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザA(H1N1)pdm09の感染拡大に関する予防啓発記事。保健省とUGMのデータに基づき陽性率上昇を報告しているが、重症度や医療体制への影響についての具体的情報は不足している。

article.articleHeadline: Rabies di Jembrana Capai 75 Kasus, Vaksinasi Emergency Dipercepat
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rabies in Jembrana Regency Reaches 75 Cases; Emergency Vaccination Accelerated.
article.articleSummary: Rabies in Jembrana Regency, Bali, reaches 75 positive cases as of September 2026, with emergency vaccination accelerated. Dinas PPP Jembrana reports 69 infected dogs, 5 cats, and 1 cow across Pangkung Gayung (Baler Bale Agung) and Banjar Moding Kaja (Candikusuma), with a rollout planned in Banjar Munduk (Pohsanten, Mendoyo). Vaccination coverage totals 33,659 of an estimated 40,310 animals (78.4%); breakdown: dogs 31,595, cats 2,043, monkeys 21. Of the 75 cases, 3 are laboratory-confirmed by BBVet Denpasar, and 28 unvaccinated animals were found in Moding (26 dogs, 2 cats). Lab-confirmed cases include a 4-month-old puppy in Baler Bale Agung, a 6-month-old dog in Pergung, and a 3-year-old wild dog in Candikusuma. Puppies can be vaccinated at 15 days with a booster after 4 weeks; adults are vaccinated annually.

triage.headline_ja: ジャンブラナ県で狂犬病75例、緊急ワクチン接種を加速
triage.triage_reason: バリ島ジャンブラナ県で動物（犬・猫・牛）の狂犬病が75例確認され拡大が続いているが、ヒトへの感染報告はなく、地元当局が緊急ワクチン接種で対応中のため、続報を注視する段階と判断。
triage.notes: 現時点ではヒト感染例の報告はなく動物間流行（犬・猫・牛）の段階。ワクチン接種率78.4%で未接種動物も残存しており、地域拡大や動物由来感染継続の可能性があるため経過観察が妥当。

article.articleHeadline: Epidemia de Ebola din RD Congo rămâne scăpată de sub control (OMS)
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo remains out of control (WHO).
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains out of control, according to the World Health Organization, as of 23 September 2026. The update highlights ongoing transmission and persistent containment challenges within DR Congo, underscoring continued risk to local populations and the need for intensified public health response. The article does not provide specific case or death counts, laboratory confirmation details, infection sources, or information on imported or exported cases, nor does it describe clinical symptoms or vaccination efforts. No additional geographic spread beyond DR Congo is mentioned. The piece frames the situation as a critical international health concern requiring sustained support from national authorities and the global community. Publication date reference: 2026-09-23; WHO remains the monitoring and guiding authority for the outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ流行、依然として制御不能な状態が続く（WHO）
triage.triage_reason: エボラは重篤な公衆衛生上の脅威であり、WHOが制御不能と評価していることから国際的拡大リスクと社会的関心が高く、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 具体的な症例数・死亡数・感染源・ワクチン接種状況等は記載なし。続報での詳細確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Dinkes Kota Malang Catat 270 Kasus Demam Berdarah hingga September 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Malang City Health Office Records 270 Dengue Fever Cases as of September 2026
article.articleSummary: 270 dengue fever cases were recorded in Malang City, Indonesia, from January to September 2026 by the Malang City Health Office (Dinkes). The count may rise by year-end, with historical data showing 462 cases in 2023, 777 in 2024, and 715 in 2025, indicating a persistent annual burden and a typical surge around March–April. Public health measures emphasize vector control through elimination of mosquito breeding sites (PSN) and intensified 3M (drain, close, recycle) and 3M Plus campaigns. Residents are urged to maintain a clean living environment year-round. Medical guidance for patients includes total rest, high fluid intake, and fever-reducing medications as prescribed; authorities warn that delayed medical care can be fatal and urge prompt hospital evaluation if symptoms persist or worsen.

triage.headline_ja: マラン市保健局、2026年9月までにデング熱270例を記録
triage.triage_reason: インドネシア・マラン市における例年発生している季節性デング熱で、過去数年と比較しても件数は少なく、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: デング熱は例年発生する疾患であり、2026年の件数（270例）は過去数年（2023年462例、2024年777例、2025年715例）より少なく、通常の季節的流行パターン内と判断される。

article.articleHeadline: Epidemia de Ebola din RD Congo nu poate fi controlată. Focarul continuă să se extindă
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo cannot be controlled. The outbreak continues to spread.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) remains out of control despite a modest decline in cases. WHO reports 7,733 confirmed infections and 3,732 deaths in the DRC, with transmission dispersing geographically and cross-border spread risk rising. The latest expansion is in the Dungu health zone of Haut-Uele province near the South Sudan border, and the epidemic has now affected 63 health zones across seven provinces. North Kivu hospital capacity is strained, with Ebola Treatment Units (ETUs) 91.2% full, and 34.2% of hospitalized patients treated outside ETUs. Nearly two-thirds of recent confirmed deaths occurred outside treatment centers. WHO regards the regional spread risk as very high in the DRC and high for neighboring countries. Declared in May, this is the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the DRC and the second-largest globally after West Africa 2014–2016.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ流行は制御不能。流行は拡大を続けている
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模のエボラ流行（感染7,733人、死亡3,732人）が継続し、国境を越えた拡大リスクが高く、医療体制も逼迫しているためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 南スーダン（Republic of the Sudan表記）およびアンゴラへの越境拡大リスクが言及されているが、両国は対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。DRCの63保健地域・7州に拡大しており、史上最大規模の流行。

article.articleHeadline: Viral Pasangan Sesama Jenis di Video Mesum A Day in My Life Terpapar HIV, Kenali HIV dan Cara Penularannya
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Viral Same-Sex Couple in the Porn Video “A Day in My Life” Exposed to HIV, Learn About HIV and How It Is Transmitted.
article.articleSummary: HIV, the Human Immunodeficiency Virus, is the focus after a viral porn video titled 'A Day in My Life' featuring a same-sex couple. In Jakarta, police confirmed that the couple depicted has HIV infection, with authorities noting the individuals previously worked in the private sector and are currently under health scrutiny. Public health experts caution that HIV transmission occurs through specific pathways: unprotected vaginal, anal, or oral sex; sharing non-sterile needles; and contaminated blood transfusions. Dr. Ngabila Salama emphasizes that infection is not caused by sexual orientation but by exposure to infectious body fluids, and urges avoiding stigma. Laboratory confirmation and further testing are needed to determine the extent and timing of transmission. As of 2026-09-23, preliminary information indicates the individuals in the video have HIV infection, prompting public health attention in Indonesia, including Jakarta and Bogor.

triage.headline_ja: バイラル動画「A Day in My Life」の同性カップル、HIV感染が判明 ― HIVの基礎知識と感染経路を解説
triage.triage_reason: 個人のHIV感染がバイラル動画を通じて話題になった事例であり、既知の疾患・既知の感染経路によるものであるため、公衆衛生上の緊急性や異常性は認められない。
triage.notes: 本記事はバイラル動画に登場する個人のHIV感染事例に関する社会的関心を扱ったもので、感染症危機管理上の新規シグナルとはみなされない。HIVは既知の疾患であり流行学的異常性はない。

article.articleHeadline: Pemkot Bandung Tingkatkan Kewaspadaan Terkait Penyebaran Kasus Influenza A
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Bandung City Government Heightens Vigilance Regarding the Spread of Influenza A Cases.
article.articleSummary: Bandung, Indonesia — The Bandung City Government has heightened vigilance for Influenza A cases, dubbed by some as 'super flu.' Mayor Muhammad Farhan urged residents not to ignore flu symptoms, especially in children, and asked health facilities to maintain elevated alert levels, comparable to COVID-19 response but at hospital/health facility scale. Isolations have occurred in some hospitalized cases, including outside Bandung. While several fatal cases have been reported outside the city, officials stress no pandemic-level response is required. Health authorities note rising case numbers but not yet highly significant; social media chatter has driven higher health facility visits and ER crowding. Parents are advised not to send children to school if flu symptoms appear—watch for high fever lasting days, loss of smell (anosmia), loss of taste (ageusia), and a prolonged, severe cough; seek medical evaluation.

triage.headline_ja: バンドン市政府、インフルエンザA型症例の拡大に関し警戒を強化
triage.triage_reason: インドネシア・バンドンで『スーパーフル』と呼ばれるインフルエンザA型の症例が増加し、死亡例も報告され、市がCOVID-19並みの警戒レベルを敷いていることから、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数項目に該当し社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 市長がCOVID-19レベルの警戒を呼びかけ、SNSでの話題化により医療機関の受診・ER混雑が増加。死亡例はバンドン市外で報告されているが詳細不明。当局はパンデミックレベルの対応は不要と述べている。

article.articleHeadline: "丰收护航 健康同行"人畜共患病防控宣传活动在宁夏吴忠启动
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: "Harvest Protection, Health Together" Public Awareness Campaign for Zoonotic Disease Prevention and Control Launched in Wuzhong, Ningxia
article.articleSummary: On 2026-09-23, during the ninth Farmers' Harvest Festival, the Chinese Center for Animal Disease Prevention and Control and Ningxia's Department of Agriculture and Rural Affairs launched the 'Harvest Protection, Health Together' zoonotic disease prevention and control campaign in Wuzhong, Ningxia, to block transmission at the source. The initiative stresses that about 60% of known infectious diseases originate in animals and highlights ongoing zoonoses risks to animals, humans, and public health. It notes national gains: glanders in horses eradicated; highly pathogenic avian influenza effectively controlled; schistosomiasis elimination progressing; echinococcosis and rabies burden reduced; brucellosis prevalence in livestock declining. Nevertheless, new and re-emerging zoonoses remain a challenge amid global disease spread and cross-species transmission. The strategy emphasizes science-driven, tech-enabled, and data-based governance with government leadership, interdepartmental collaboration, public participation, and multi-stakeholder co-governance to curb transmission.

triage.headline_ja: 「収穫を守り、健康を共に」人畜共通感染症予防管理啓発活動が寧夏回族自治区呉忠市で始動
triage.triage_reason: 特定の疾病アウトブレイクの報告ではなく、人畜共通感染症予防に関する広報・啓発キャンペーンの開始を伝える一般的な政策記事であるため。
triage.notes: 記事は具体的な感染症の発生・流行を報じるものではなく、中国政府による人畜共通感染症予防の広報キャンペーン開始に関する内容。狂馬鼻疽の撲滅、鳥インフルエンザの制御、住血吸虫症・エキノコックス症・狂犬病・ブルセラ症の減少など、既存の成果を紹介する政策的トーンの記事。

article.articleHeadline: पशुओं में फिर मंडराया लम्पी स्किन का खतरा:LUVAS की चेतावनी- समय पर कराएं टीकाकरण, लापरवाही पड़ सकती है भारी
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Threat of Lumpy Skin Disease looms again among livestock: LUVAS warns—Vaccinate on time; negligence could prove costly.
article.articleSummary: Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD) threatens cows and other bovines in India as Lala Lajpat Rai Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (LUVAS) in Hisar issues a detailed advisory (Chandigarh dateline). LSDV, a member of the Poxviridae family and Capripoxvirus genus, spreads among bovines. The disease presents with skin nodules, enlarged lymph nodes, and swelling around limbs, lower abdomen, and udders, accompanied by high fever, loss of appetite, extreme weakness, rapid weight loss, sharply reduced milk yield, and infertility. If dehydration or secondary infections occur, the illness can be severe and fatal. Immediate actions include isolating affected animals, notifying the veterinary department, and burying dead animals in deep pits. Timely vaccination of healthy animals is strongly advised to prevent outbreaks. The advisory underscores prompt recognition and preventive vaccination to mitigate costs and spread.

triage.headline_ja: 家畜に再びランピースキン病の脅威:LUVASが警告—時期を逃さぬワクチン接種を、怠れば大きな代償に
triage.triage_reason: 動物（牛）のみに影響する家畜疾病に関する予防的注意喚起であり、ヒトへの公衆衛生上の脅威や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 本疾患（ランピースキン病）はウシ科動物のみに感染するウイルス性疾患で、人獣共通感染症ではない。獣医大学による予防的アドバイザリー記事であり、ヒト公衆衛生上のリスクはないためDISMISS。

article.articleHeadline: Rubella Virus Detected In Jharkhand; Know Symptoms And Prevention
article.articleSummary: Rubella virus detected in Jharkhand; first case of the season. A 10-year-old girl from Thethai­tangar block in Simdega district has tested positive, prompting enhanced surveillance and vaccination efforts. Rubella, or German measles, is a contagious viral infection spread mainly through respiratory droplets. Many infections are mild or asymptomatic, but who are infectious may transmit the virus before and after rash onset. When present, symptoms include a red rash beginning on the face and spreading, low-grade fever, sore throat, headache, runny nose, mild conjunctivitis and swollen lymph nodes; diagnosis may require testing. Pregnancy poses a serious risk: infection in early pregnancy can lead to miscarriage, fetal death, or congenital rubella syndrome. Prevention relies on vaccination, particularly the rubella-containing MMR vaccine, which is about 97% effective after one dose. There is no specific antiviral treatment; management is supportive. Emphasizes vaccination and immunity checks for women planning pregnancy.

triage.headline_ja: ジャールカンド州で風疹ウイルスを検出；症状と予防法について
triage.triage_reason: インド・ジャールカンド州における単発の風疹症例報告であり、既知の疾患で季節性の初発例に過ぎず、公衆衛生上の重大な影響や異常性、国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 風疹は既知のワクチン予防可能疾患であり、単発症例の報告のため通常のサーベイランス範囲内と判断。妊婦への注意喚起が主目的の一般向け医療情報記事。

article.articleHeadline: Maniema : plus de 10 cas suspects de choléra recensés à l'hôpital général de Kindu
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Maniema: More than 10 suspected cholera cases recorded at Kindu General Hospital.
article.articleSummary: Cholera is suspected in Maniema, Democratic Republic of Congo, with 13 suspected cases currently under care at Kindu General Referral Hospital as of 22–23 September 2026. Dr. Famba Ramazani Jean, the hospital’s medical director, reported that samples have been collected and laboratory analyses are awaited to confirm or rule out cholera; while patients show signs compatible with cholera, no official confirmation can be made until biological results are available. The competent authority will declare actual cases if confirmed. In the interim, authorities urge the public to reinforce hygiene: drink potable water, wash hands regularly, use latrines properly, and consume well-cooked foods. Residents are advised to remain vigilant and strictly observe preventive measures to limit potential spread during pending confirmation.

triage.headline_ja: マニエマ州:キンドゥ総合病院でコレラ疑い例が10人以上確認
triage.triage_reason: コレラ疑い13例が報告されているが、検査結果待ちで未確定。DRCはコレラの風土病地域であり異常性は低いが、水系感染症としての拡大可能性があるため続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 検査結果未確定のため、確定例が報告され次第フルRRAへの移行を検討すべき。DRCはコレラ常在国であり過去にも流行歴あり。

article.articleHeadline: Ada 700 Kasus Gigitan HPR pada Manusia di Jembrana, Hingga September Ada 75 Kasus Rabies pada Hewan
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: There Are 700 HPR Bite Cases in Humans in Jembrana; As of September There Are 75 Rabies Cases in Animals.
article.articleSummary: As of August 31, 2026, Jembrana, Bali reports about 5,622 human bites from rabies-exposure (HPR) cases Jan–Aug, averaging roughly 700 per month. Rabies-positive animals total 75 across 69 dogs, 5 cats, and 1 cow, with most cases in Mendoyo and Negara districts. Health authorities confirm ongoing human exposure risk despite vaccine stock: vaccines and rabies immune serum remain sufficient through year-end 2026, supported by the provincial and central health ministries. Vaccination progress has reached 78.4% of the estimated reservoir population: over 31,000 dogs, about 2,000 cats, and 21 monkeys vaccinated. Experts note rapid dog breeding accelerates population growth, contributing to new cases, many involving unvaccinated puppies. Three newly confirmed animal cases were reported last weekend.

triage.headline_ja: ジェンバラナ県で人へのHPR咬傷700件、9月までに動物の狂犬病75件確認
triage.triage_reason: バリ島ジェンバラナ県で狂犬病媒介動物による咬傷と動物の陽性例が継続的に発生しているが、地域内で流行している疾患であり、ワクチン供給は十分とされ、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 狂犬病はバリ島（ジェンバラナ県含む）で地域流行状態にあり、当局はワクチン在庫が2026年末まで十分と確認済み。ヒト死亡例の記載はなく、動物間・動物-ヒト間の継続的曝露リスクが中心の内容。

article.articleHeadline: NCDC Releases Advisory On Ebola, Says Nigeria On 'High Alert'
article.articleSummary: Nigeria’s NCDC issued a health advisory after the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s ongoing Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreak, placing Nigeria on high alert with ongoing preparedness. Travelers from countries with active EVD transmission must complete a Health Declaration Form; passengers from other countries are exempt. The public is advised to stay vigilant for EVD symptoms and promptly seek medical care, reporting travel or exposure history. The advisory stems from dynamic risk assessment and consultations with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare. As of 20 September 2026, the DRC reported 7,672 confirmed EVD cases and 3,699 related deaths; 886 patients are in isolation (up 58 cases and 23 deaths since 19 September). New case distribution: Ituri 38, North Kivu 14, Haut-Uélé 5, Tshopo 1. Bundibugyo virus infections: 1,879 recovered. About 79.9% of identified contacts remain under follow-up. Since 18 September, the ECDC logged 197 additional cases and 94 deaths.

triage.headline_ja: NCDC、エボラ出血熱に関する勧告を発表 ナイジェリアは「厳戒態勢」と表明
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で継続中のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクが大規模（確定7,672例、死亡3,699例）で、国境を越えた拡大リスクからナイジェリアが渡航者への健康申告を義務付けるなど対応を強化しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はDRCで継続中のエボラアウトブレイクであり、ナイジェリアは対象国リストに含まれないため予防的な勧告発出国として除外した。Bundibugyoウイルス感染例（1,879例回復）も併記されているが、主要な公衆衛生上の懸念はDRCのエボラ拡大である。

article.articleHeadline: Kasus Super Flu Terdeteksi di 13 Provinsi, Begini Bahayanya - tvOnenews
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Super Flu Cases Detected in 13 Provinces, Here's How Dangerous It Is
article.articleSummary: Influenza A(H3N2) subclade K, nicknamed 'Superflu', has been detected in 13 Indonesian provinces since January 2026. The heaviest burden is in East Java and South Kalimantan, each with 18 cases; West Java has 12, Jakarta 11. Other affected provinces include South Sumatra, North Sumatra, Bali, East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara, North Sulawesi, Central Java, South Sulawesi, and the Special Region of Yogyakarta. In week-36 surveillance, 185 specimens were tested; 86 were positive for influenza: 76 A(H1N1)pdm09, 8 A(H3N2), and 2 B Victoria. The report emphasizes that H3N2 is part of seasonal influenza and the 'Superflu' label does not reflect a new virus. Public health guidance remains to monitor symptoms (fever, cough, runny nose, malaise, body aches), protect vulnerable groups, practice hygiene, cough etiquette, and wear masks when symptomatic. Overall influenza activity remains low.

triage.headline_ja: スーパーフル症例が13州で検出、その危険性とは - tvOnenews
triage.triage_reason: インドネシア13州でH3N2亜系統Kが検出され『スーパーフル』として話題化しているが、当局は季節性インフルエンザの範疇であり新規ウイルスではないと説明しており、全体の陽性率・活動レベルは低い。ただし複数州への拡大とメディアの注目度から継続的な観察が必要。
triage.notes: 記事は『スーパーフル』という名称が誤解を招くセンセーショナルな表現であることを強調し、実態は季節性インフルエンザ（主にH1N1pdm09が優勢）であると説明している。重症度・死亡例等の具体的情報はなく、当局は監視を継続中としている。

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Krishnagiri, dengue affects 320 people, and 85 people have Unni fever: Collector reports.
article.articleSummary: Dengue has affected 320 people in Krishnagiri district, Tamil Nadu this week, with 139 cases of leptospirosis (rat fever) and 85 cases of Unni fever, according to District Collector S. Dinesh Kumar. A two-week district-wide intensive cleanliness drive has been launched to curb mosquito- and rodent-borne diseases, prompted by standing rainwater, pools, garbage and unsanitary surroundings. Before the monsoon, 7,094 public places—government buildings, schools, colleges, Anganwadi centers, hostels and factories—will receive structural cleaning. Tasks include roof cleaning, waste removal, draining stagnant water, clearing gutters, chlorination, ensuring safe drinking water, and sealing breeding sites. Each building will have an assigned officer, and private factories must report with photographic evidence. The objective is to eradicate breeding sites and safeguard health through interdepartmental coordination. Attendees at the review included Osur Municipal Commissioner Mohammed Shabir Alam, district rural development director Uma Maheswari, district health officer Jeganathan, municipal health officer Ajita and other officials.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: NCDC to screen travellers from affected countries
article.articleSummary: Travelers from countries with active or relevant Ebola Virus Disease transmission may be required to complete Health Declaration Forms as Nigeria's NCDC issues an interim public health advisory amid the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The measure aims to strengthen importation prevention through enhanced surveillance and follow-up. Passengers from other countries are currently exempt. The advisory, signed by NCDC Director-General Dr Jide Idris, reflects evolving epidemiology and public health consultations with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare. Nigerians are urged to remain vigilant for symptoms consistent with Ebola and to seek medical attention promptly, reporting travel or exposure history where applicable. Nigeria remains on high alert with ongoing preparedness activities, and these measures will be reviewed as the epidemiological situation changes to maintain protection against imported or secondary cases.

triage.notes: 記事の主題はDRCでのエボラ流行とそれに対するナイジェリアの渡航者スクリーニング対応。ナイジェリアは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。DRCでの流行状況（症例数・死亡者数等）の詳細情報が不足しており、続報での確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 国家卫生健康委：秦岭淮河以南地区蚊虫仍较活跃 需警惕虫媒传染病
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: National Health Commission: Mosquitoes Still Active in Regions South of the Qinling–Huaihe Line; Vigilance for Vector-borne Infectious Diseases Is Needed
article.articleSummary: Mosquitoes remain active south of the Qinling–Huaihe Line as autumn arrives, with warmer temperatures and higher rainfall sustaining vector activity, according to a National Health Commission briefing referencing China CDC. Dengue fever, chikungunya fever, and malaria pose ongoing risks; travelers should check destination disease trends, understand protections and emergency measures, and carry effective anti-mosquito products. For malaria-prone regions, consult professionals and adopt preventive measures. After returning from dengue or malaria areas, monitor health for up to one month; fever, chills, sweating, rash, or joint pain should prompt medical care and disclosure of travel history, and continued mosquito precautions may be needed if local vectors persist to prevent secondary spread. Home and personal protection include eliminating standing water in flower pots, buckets, and containers; installing screens or nets; wearing long clothing; and using approved repellents, with protection needed day and night due to varying mosquito activity times.

article.articleHeadline: 7 Hal yang Harus Dilakukan Saat Hujan Pertama Setelah Kemarau, Cegah DBD hingga Atap Bocor - merdeka.com
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 7 Things to Do During the First Rain After the Dry Season, Prevent Dengue Fever and Leaky Roofs
article.articleSummary: First rain after the dry season in Indonesia heightens dengue fever risk as Aedes aegypti mosquitoes breed in standing water. Practical guidance emphasizes home and road safety. Before heavy rains, clean gutters, drains, and roofs to prevent overflow. Inspect roofs, flashing, and joints for leaks and seal or replace damaged sections. Roads become unusually slick due to residual oil and dust; motorists should slow down, use headlights, maintain safe distances, and ensure tires and brakes are in good condition. After the rain, wash vehicles promptly to remove dust and pollutants that can dull paint and corrode metal; check undercarriages, brakes, and electricals, especially for motorcycles. During the seasonal transition, authorities warn that standing water fosters dengue-carrying Aedes aegypti, raising dengue fever risk in Indonesia.

article.articleHeadline: Tamil Nadu government advises vulnerable groups to wear masks amid rise in dengue cases
article.articleSummary: Tamil Nadu: 301 fresh dengue cases in a single day raise the year total to 17,649 with 9 deaths as of 23 September 2026. Authorities intensified field measures across the state, including door-to-door inspections to curb mosquito breeding and reduce stagnant water around homes. The Health and Family Welfare Department advises fever patients and vulnerable groups—pregnant women, senior citizens, people with low immunity, and children with fever—to wear masks as a precaution; usage is not mandatory. Parents are urged not to send feverish children to school. Residents are encouraged to eliminate standing water and seek medical evaluation promptly for fever or cough. The advisory aims to mitigate dengue transmission while addressing broader respiratory infection risks.

triage.triage_reason: インド・タミルナードゥ州でのデング熱は季節性流行の範囲内だが、症例急増と死亡者発生、当局による異例のマスク着用勧告があり、経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: デング熱はインドで毎年発生する季節性感染症であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低いが、症例数・死亡者数の推移とマスク着用勧告という異例の対応は注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Dinas Kesehatan Lampung Temukan Kasus Influenza A H1N1 Musiman
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Lampung Health Office Detects Seasonal Influenza A (H1N1) Cases.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 continues as part of seasonal influenza in Lampung Province, Indonesia, with surveillance data through Sept 21, 2026. The Ministry of Health reports a rising proportion of positive influenza specimens nationwide in September 2026, with A(H1N1)pdm09 as the most dominant subtype. Lampung ranks fifth nationally and second in Sumatra for influenza cases. Sentinel surveillance across health facilities detected 10 influenza-positive cases: 4 A(H1N1)pdm09 and 6 A(H3N2); no other A subtypes (H5N1, H7N9, H9N2) or influenza B detected; COVID-19 not detected in ILI data. In Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI), 3 influenza positives are all A(H3N2); A(H1N1)pdm09 not detected in SARI. Officials emphasize that A(H1N1)pdm09 is not a new pandemic virus but a persistent seasonal subtype; vigilance remains due to potential severe outcomes in certain groups. Data derive from sentinel facilities and may not reflect total community cases.

article.articleHeadline: 40 Ribu Warga Jatim Terjangkit Wabah Influenza A, Begini Kondisinya
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 40,000 East Java Residents Infected by Influenza A Outbreak, Here’s Their Condition.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A outbreak in East Java, Indonesia, with more than 40,000 residents infected from January through August, according to Surabaya Health Office. The tally rose again from August into September, about a 10% uptick, with cases predominantly mild—fever, weakness, and cough. Surabaya Health Office head Dr. Billy Messakh notes the pattern aligns with Influenza A activity. East Java Deputy Governor Emil Dardak says hospitals have not been overwhelmed as of September 23, 2026, and health services remain on alert to anticipate further surges. Indonesia’s Ministry of Health reports Influenza A H3N2 subclade K detected in 13 provinces nationwide. Transmission occurs via respiratory droplets from coughing, sneezing, or talking, with higher risk in crowded settings. The illness remains a concern for vulnerable groups, and is distinguished from common colds.

article.articleHeadline: 中秋国庆假期 注意防范手足口病、诺如病毒病
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: During the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays, take precautions to prevent hand-foot-and-mouth disease and norovirus infection.
article.articleSummary: China faces ongoing risk of hand-foot-mouth disease and norovirus during the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays; prior infections do not guarantee immunity. Authorities urge intensified hygiene, food safety, and protection as travel increases. Entry hygiene: wash hands with soap or sanitizer and running water for at least 20 seconds; norovirus is not fully inactivated by alcohol-based sanitizers; avoid untreated water and undercooked foods; seafood and shellfish should be cooked. Promptly disinfect areas contaminated by vomiting or diarrhea and avoid food preparation during illness. Respiratory precautions: ensure ventilation in hotels and venues; wear masks in crowded or poorly ventilated spaces; cough and sneeze etiquette. Vaccination: elderly, children, and chronically ill individuals should get influenza vaccine; antibodies develop in 2–4 weeks, ideally before the flu season. Health monitoring: seek medical care for fever, rash, vomiting, or diarrhea and disclose travel history. HPV vaccination for 13-year-old girls should be completed per policy.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Growing problem of H1N1 swine flu in children; get the influenza vaccine to protect against the flu.
article.articleSummary: As of 23 September 2026, H1N1 influenza (swine flu) is rising among children in Varanasi, India. Typical symptoms include high fever, runny nose, cough, chills, and sometimes vomiting or diarrhea. Paracetamol should be given every 6–8 hours; if fever persists beyond two days, seek a pediatrician for influenza testing and treatment. An influenza vaccine is available, with the first dose at six months and the second dose after four weeks; reinforce prevention with regular handwashing and mask use. Other febrile illnesses this season include dengue, malaria, scrub typhus, leptospirosis, and typhoid, diagnosed via blood tests and treated with targeted medications. In OPD, vomiting and diarrhea from viral or bacterial infections are common and managed with antiemetic, ORS, and paracetamol; breastfeeding should continue. The article also notes dengue IgM/NS1 testing and chikungunya RT-PCR testing among children.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue fever intensifies in Madurai - more than 40 people affected!
article.articleSummary: On 23 September 2026, dengue fever intensifies in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, with more than 100 people hospitalized for dengue or viral fever across government and private facilities as the northeast monsoon begins. In Madurai district, 3 dengue cases are confirmed in the Madurai Government Medical College hospital’s dengue ward, while over 40 patients are being treated for viral fever; blood samples are sent for dengue confirmation. Authorities have intensified vector-control within Madurai Corporation limits (about 100 wards), including mosquito spraying and inspections of water tanks, stagnant water sites, discarded containers, tires, and other water-collecting items. Awareness drives and home vector-control measures cover over 50,000 households. More than 75 official teams are conducting surveys; schools, colleges, and hostels are included in inspections and spraying. The Health Department reports daily medical camps exceeding 100 locations; for urgent assistance, call 104.

article.articleHeadline: 46 người ngộ độc ở Quảng Trị: Phát hiện vi khuẩn trong mẫu bệnh phẩm bánh mì
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 46 people poisoned in Quang Tri: Bacteria detected in bread samples.
article.articleSummary: Salmonella outbreak linked to a newly opened bakery in Cam Lộ Commune, Quảng Trị Province, Vietnam, sickened 46 people who ate bread products. On 23 September 2026, Quảng Trị's Food Safety Authority said tests by Pasteur Institute Nha Trang found Salmonella spp in 9 of 11 food samples and in 11 of 13 patient specimens; one patient sample carried both Salmonella spp and Staphylococcus aureus. Contaminated items included beef sausage, fish sausage, vegetables, braised meat, pickles, cucumber, bread, and sandwiches. All 46 patients were treated at Cam Lộ Regional General Hospital and discharged by the afternoon of 22 September in stable condition. Authorities ordered the M.T bakery to halt operations pending ongoing investigation.

triage.notes: 疾患名がParatyphoid/Typhoidと分類されているが、記事内容はSalmonella属菌による食中毒（食品由来の集団食中毒）であり、腸チフス・パラチフスとは異なる。地域はクアンチ省カムロー社の一ベーカリーに限定された局所事例。

article.articleHeadline: 'கொத்து கொத்தாக குவியும் டெங்கு நோயாளிகள்' காணாமல் போன சுகாதாரத்துறை அமைச்சர் அருண்ராஜ்..!
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 'Dengue patients piling up in heaps' Health Minister Arunraj goes missing..!
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever is surging in Tamil Nadu, with 17,649 dengue patients admitted and 9 deaths reported as of 23 September 2026. Daily dengue admissions have topped 300. In Chennai, 614 dengue cases were recorded in the first 18 days of September; by 16 September, Tamil Nadu logged 283 cases, up from 61 on 14 September. The outbreak coincides with monsoon rains creating standing water and increased mosquito breeding. Authorities warn of further rises in coming months. Health Minister Arunraj, an IAS officer and physician, is the Dharapuram by-election in-charge and has been stationed in Dharapuram for over a week, focusing on campaigning amid criticism of inadequate containment. Aspayar Ramasami, administrator of the Annamalai organization, criticized the government for inaction and urged urgent preventive measures. August dengue cases rose 66% year-on-year.

triage.notes: デング熱はインドの風土病だが、モンスーン期の急増（前年比66%増、死亡9名）と保健大臣への批判が社会的関心を高めている。国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは記事からは確認できない。

article.articleHeadline: 中疾控：诺如病毒对酒精不敏感，免洗洗手液不能替代流水洗手
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: China CDC: Norovirus is not sensitive to alcohol; hand sanitizers cannot replace handwashing with running water.
article.articleSummary: Norovirus is not sensitive to alcohol and hand sanitizers cannot replace handwashing with running water. Immunity to norovirus or hand-foot-mouth disease (HFMD) is not guaranteed; reinfection can occur for both. During the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays in China, the China CDC urged continued emphasis on hand hygiene, food safety, and personal protection. Wash hands with running water using soap or detergent for at least 20 seconds; alcohol-based sanitizers cannot substitute for water washing when dealing with norovirus. Do not drink untreated water or consume raw or undercooked foods; seafood and shellfish should be thoroughly cooked. If a household member has vomiting or diarrhea, promptly disinfect contaminated surfaces and items; ill individuals should not prepare food for others. More guidance is available via the Beijing Daily App.

article.articleHeadline: 46 người nhập viện sau ăn bánh mì: Nhiều mẫu thực phẩm dương tính Salmonella spp
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 46 people hospitalized after eating bánh mì sandwiches: Many food samples tested positive for Salmonella spp.
article.articleSummary: 46 people were hospitalized after eating bánh mì sandwiches in Cam Lộ, Quảng Trị Province, Vietnam, on Sept 14–15, 2026. Pasteur Institute Nha Trang detected Salmonella spp in 9 of 11 food samples, including beef sausage, fish sausage, vegetables, braised meat, pickled vegetables, cucumber, bread, sandwiches, and a beverage. Of 13 patient samples, 11 were positive for Salmonella spp, with one sample also yielding Staphylococcus aureus. Symptoms reported include diarrhea, abdominal pain, fever, nausea, and vomiting. The implicated food establishment was suspended and the Cam Lộ Commune authorities were tasked with investigating possible links between the foods and illnesses. By Sept 22, the 46 hospitalized patients had stabilized and were discharged; no deaths were reported. An ongoing investigation seeks to identify the infection source and any connection between the food samples and cases.

triage.headline_ja: バインミー(サンドイッチ)を食べた後46人が入院：多くの食品サンプルからサルモネラ属菌が陽性
triage.triage_reason: ベトナム国内の一地域で発生した食中毒（サルモネラ）事案であり、患者は全員回復・退院し死者もない。国際的拡大リスクや異常性は認められず、疾患タグ（腸チフス/パラチフス）は記事内容と一致しない誤タグと判断される。
triage.notes: 疾患名タグは'Paratyphoid/Typhoid'だが、記事内容は食品由来のサルモネラ属菌（Salmonella spp）による食中毒事案であり、腸チフス菌（Salmonella Typhi）とは異なる。原因施設は営業停止となり、患者は全員回復済み。ヒト-ヒト感染の可能性は低く、単発の食品汚染事案とみられる。

article.articleHeadline: Kasus Meningkat di Indonesia, Puskemas Way Halim II Belum Terima Pasien Influenza Terbaru
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cases on the Rise in Indonesia, Way Halim II Community Health Center Has Not Yet Received Latest Influenza Patients
article.articleSummary: On September 2026, Indonesia’s Ministry of Health reported an uptick in the proportion of influenza-positive specimens nationwide, with influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 identified as the dominant subtype. In Bandar Lampung, at Way Halim II Community Health Center (Puskesmas Way Halim II), staff observed routine service activities on Sept 23, 2026, but there had not yet been any confirmed influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 cases; patients presenting were reporting common flu-like symptoms. Eko of Puskesmas Way Halim II said there is no confirmed A(H1N1)pdm09 case at the facility and advised inquiries be directed to the Health Department, specifically the division handling prevention and control of communicable diseases, for case counts and details on the disease and preventive measures. The Health Ministry noted Lampung province ranks among the nation’s top five, reflecting the regional rise in positive influenza specimens.

triage.headline_ja: インドネシアで症例増加、ワイ・ハリムII保健所は最新のインフルエンザ患者を未だ受け入れず
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザA(H1N1)pdm09の陽性率上昇が報告されているが、重症度や地域拡大の詳細情報が不足しており、当該保健所では確定症例がまだない段階である。
triage.notes: H1N1pdm09は季節性インフルエンザの既知の亜型であり、新規性・異常性は低い。ランプン州は陽性検体増加の上位5州とされるが、重症度・死亡者数等の詳細は記事に記載なし。続報での症例数や重症度情報の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: சென்னையில் வேகமெடுக்கும் காய்ச்சல்: காய்ச்சல் வந்தா உடனே என்ன பண்ணனும்? டாக்டர் சொல்லும் முக்கிய அறிவுரைகள்!
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Fever on the Rise in Chennai: What to Do Immediately When Fever Strikes? Important Advice from Doctors!
article.articleSummary: As of mid-September 2026 in Tamil Nadu, dengue cases reach 16,577 with 9 deaths, while Chennai reports about 4,600 fever cases this month. Fever surges follow monsoon rains; fever alone does not prove dengue. Influenza, malaria, typhoid, and other infections can cause similar illness, with mosquitoes thriving in stagnant water after rain. Dr. Prasanna Karthik S. of CleenClinix Medical notes fever management hinges on symptoms and timely evaluation. Do: stay hydrated, rest, monitor symptoms; seek testing for persistent or severe signs (breathlessness, vomiting, severe abdominal pain, confusion, bleeding, reduced urination); ensure safe drinking water and food; practice hand hygiene and mosquito protection; avoid crowded places if fever or respiratory symptoms appear. Don’t: self-medicate with antibiotics or assume dengue without confirmation. Fever is a symptom requiring medical diagnosis.

triage.headline_ja: チェンナイで発熱が急増：発熱時にすぐすべきことは？医師が教える重要なアドバイス
triage.triage_reason: タミルナードゥ州でのデング熱等季節性発熱の増加は既知の季節性流行パターンであり突発的異常性は低いが、症例規模（16,577件、9死亡）は継続監視に値するため。
triage.notes: 記事は医師による発熱対処法の啓発記事であり、デング熱・インフルエンザ・マラリア・腸チフス等の鑑別を促す内容。モンスーン後の季節性発熱増加は例年見られるパターンであり、新規性・異常性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Kapolda Jateng Kunjungi Puskesmas Adiwerna Tegal, Tinjau Skrining Tuberkulosis
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Central Java Police Chief Visits Adiwerna Community Health Center, Tegal, Inspects Tuberculosis Screening
article.articleSummary: TB screening and examination at Puskesmas Adiwerna, Kabupaten Tegal, Central Java, were reviewed by Central Java Police Chief Irjen Pol Ribut Hari Wibowo on 23 September 2026. The visit covered sputum testing, free chest X-ray, and Active Case Finding (ACF) contact tracing for tuberculosis patients, as part of ongoing efforts to detect TB earlier. The event featured collaboration with the Dinas Kesehatan (health office), PPTI, and local police, with 80 recipients receiving care packages. The police emphasized the use of TOSS TB (Temukan Obati Sampai Sembuh Tuberkulosis) to strengthen tracing through Bhabinkamtibmas working with health workers to identify contacts and encourage screening and treatment. Awards were given to two Bhabinkamtibmas, Aipda Andrieas Eka and Bripda Toto Yuniarto, for leading TB contact tracing efforts.

triage.headline_ja: 中部ジャワ州警察本部長、テガル県アディウェルナ保健所を訪問し結核スクリーニングを視察
triage.triage_reason: 既存の結核対策プログラムの通常活動を報じるもので、異常な公衆衛生事象や新規アウトブレイクの情報はない。
triage.notes: 地域の結核対策プログラム（TOSS TB）の啓発活動・スクリーニング実施報告であり、通常の公衆衛生活動報道。

article.articleHeadline: Jaga Ketahanan Pangan dan Cegah Penyakit Hewan Masuk Pangkalpinang, Pemkot Gandeng Balai Karantina
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: City Government Partners with Quarantine Office to Maintain Food Security and Prevent Animal Diseases from Entering Pangkalpinang
article.articleSummary: Pangkalpinang city government, through the Food and Agriculture Service (Dispaper), strengthens coordination with the Balai Karantina Hewan, Ikan dan Tumbuhan Kepulauan Bangka Belitung to safeguard food security and prevent entry of animal and plant diseases. The Municipal Dinas visited the quarantine office; Acting Head Mashur Samsuri noted supervision of animal and plant movements into Pangkalpinang, emphasizing the rabies-free status and the aim to maintain it. Balai Karantina Chief Herwintarti welcomed the collaboration, stating quarantine aids a more autonomous regional food system. The partnership has opened export opportunities for Pangkalpinang commodities such as ketapang leaves, mangosteen leaves, and pine fruits, with shipments to Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States. The initiative links public health with agricultural resilience and international market access.

triage.headline_ja: 食料安全保障の維持と動物疾病侵入防止のため、パンカルピナン市政府が検疫局と連携
triage.triage_reason: 狂犬病の発生は報告されておらず、むしろ狂犬病フリー状態の維持に関する行政連携の記事であり、公衆衛生上の懸念は認められない。
triage.notes: 記事は狂犬病の発生事例ではなく、検疫体制強化と農産物輸出促進に関する行政広報記事。狂犬病フリー状態の維持が言及されているのみ。

article.articleHeadline: Virus Ebola : la Tunisie envoie une aide médicale à la République démocratique du Congo - Tunisie Numerique
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola virus: Tunisia sends medical aid to the Democratic Republic of the Congo - Tunisie Numerique
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo prompts international aid. On 22 September 2026, Tunisia dispatched a large in-kind cargo—medicines and medical and paramedical supplies—to support Congolese authorities amid the Ebola spread. The operation was coordinated by Tunisia’s Foreign Affairs, Migration, and Tunisian Abroad ministries, along with the Defence, Health, and Social Affairs ministries, the Tunisian Red Crescent, and the Tunisian Union of Solidarity. Loading and transport were overseen by the Ministry of National Defence, with the cargo carried by a Tunisian military aircraft to Kinshasa International Airport. The Tunisian embassy in Kinshasa will hand over the aid to Congolese authorities. The action, ordered by the Tunisian president, aligns with Africa-wide solidarity and responds to the African Union’s call to bolster Congo’s health system; no case counts are provided.

triage.headline_ja: エボラウイルス：チュニジアがコンゴ民主共和国に医療支援を派遣
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ発生に対し国際的な医療支援が実施されており、IHR基準（深刻性・異常性・国際的拡大）に複数該当する。既知の高リスク病原体であり、フルRRAへの移行が適切。
triage.notes: 記事はチュニジアからのDRC向け医療支援輸送を報じるもので、DRC国内の感染者数や発生地域の詳細（キンシャサ以外への拡大有無等）は記載されていない。エボラという病原体特性から高リスクと判断したが、症例数・致死率等の詳細情報は続報で確認が必要。チュニジア自体は感染発生国ではなく支援国のため対象国リストに含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Khuẩn Salmonella trong bánh mì khiến hơn 40 người ở Quảng Trị ngộ độc
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Salmonella bacteria in bread sickens more than 40 people in Quảng Trị Province.
article.articleSummary: Salmonella enterica infection linked to a bread shop in Cam Lộ commune, Quảng Trị Province, Vietnam. Since 15 September, more than 40 customers developed fever, chills, severe abdominal pain, vomiting and diarrhea after consuming bread products. Pasteur Institute Nha Trang confirmed Salmonella in 9 of 11 food samples taken at the bakery and in 11 of 13 patient specimens; one patient was co-infected with Staphylococcus aureus. Two patient samples were negative. The Quảng Trị Food Safety Sub-Department has forwarded the case file to Cam Lộ Commune authorities to trace the link between ingredients and illness and to implement containment measures. All affected patients have been discharged. This is the second bread-related outbreak in Quảng Trị within four months; a May incident sickened over 80 people and resulted in fines for origin-ingredient violations.

triage.headline_ja: パンに含まれるサルモネラ菌によりクアンチ省で40人以上が食中毒
triage.triage_reason: 単一パン屋を起因とする食中毒事例で、患者は全員退院済み。ヒト-ヒト感染や国際的拡大の可能性はなく、地方当局で対応可能な事案。
triage.notes: 同地域で4ヶ月以内に2回目のパン関連食中毒事例（5月にも80人超が発症）。国内食品安全管理の課題として地方当局が対応中だが、国際的な公衆衛生上の懸念は低い。

article.articleHeadline: RSUD Diisukan Penuh Akibat Merbaknya Influenza A, Dinkes Surabaya Bongkar Fakta Sebenarnya
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Regional General Hospital Rumored to Be Full Due to the Spread of Influenza A, Surabaya Health Office Reveals the Truth
article.articleSummary: Influenza A is not causing hospital overflow in Surabaya. The Surabaya City Health Office says inpatient capacity at RSUD Dr. Mohammad Soewandhie and RSUD Eka Candrarini remains adequate, debunking rumors of a full Regional General Hospital. Mayor Eri Cahyadi directs city hospitals to coordinate and ensure medical staff readiness. Influenza A symptoms resemble typical flu with low fatality, and no deaths reported; ISPA and flu cases have risen about 10–15% from January–August to September, but remain within normal ranges and do not require COVID-like intensive care. Treatment follows standard flu care; no need for excessive strain differentiation. Preventive measures include staying calm, maintaining immunity (rest, balanced diet, vitamin C), and wearing masks in crowds or enclosed spaces, especially when unwell. Vaccination for influenza is advised at local health facilities. ISPA symptoms (cough, sneeze, fever, fatigue) should prompt rest and a visit to the nearest Puskesmas if symptoms persist.

triage.headline_ja: 病院が満床という噂はインフルエンザA流行によるものと報道、スラバヤ保健局が真相を明らかに
triage.triage_reason: スラバヤ保健局が病院満床の噂を否定し、症例数は季節的な範囲内で重症例や死亡例もなく、通常のインフルエンザ対応で管理可能と説明している。
triage.notes: 記事は病院満床の噂に対する行政の否定・説明が主旨であり、インフルエンザ自体は季節性の範囲内で重症化や死亡もないため公衆衛生上の懸念は低い。

article.articleHeadline: 安特羅攜泰國Biogenetech，腸病毒EV71疫苗搶攻300萬嬰幼兒市場
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Antero teams up with Thailand's Biogenetech to vie for the EV71 vaccine market for 3 million infants and young children.
article.articleSummary: Antero Biotech signs an exclusive Thailand distribution deal with Biogenetech to launch its Enterovirus 71 (EV71) vaccine in Thailand, targeting about 3 million infants and young children in self-pay and public tender markets. Biogenetech, a local firm with over 30 years of experience, will leverage its cold-chain logistics, hospital and private clinic networks, government tender expertise, and local KOLs to support regulatory registration and commercialization. EV71 is neurotropic and can cause encephalitis and cardiopulmonary failure; Thailand’s surveillance shows 94,670 hand-foot-mouth disease cases in 2025 (Jan–Sep), with EV71 accounting for about 18–19% of tests, indicating ongoing demand. Thailand’s 0–4 age group at risk is about 2.64 million, with 400,000 births annually, suggesting strong market potential when combined with self-pay and public funding. Antero aims to obtain regulatory approval and launch the vaccine, expanding Southeast Asia vaccine commercialization through local partnerships.

triage.headline_ja: 安特羅、タイのBiogenetechと提携しEV71（エンテロウイルス71型）ワクチンで幼児300万人市場を狙う
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はワクチン販売提携に関する商業ニュースであり、具体的な感染急増やアウトブレイクの報告ではないため、シグナルとしての要件を満たさない。
triage.notes: 記事はタイにおけるEV71ワクチンの商業展開に関するもので、2025年のHFMDサーベイランスデータ（94,670例、EV71が18-19%）は市場背景として言及されているのみ。急性のアウトブレイクや異常事象の報告はない。

article.articleHeadline: இவர்களெல்லாம் மாஸ்க் அணிவது அவசியம்" - டெங்கு பரவலை தடுக்க முக்கிய அறிவுரை!
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: "All of them must wear a mask" - Important advice to prevent the spread of dengue!
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever is rising in Tamil Nadu, India. As of 23 September 2026, officials report 301 new dengue infections confirmed yesterday, elevating the year’s total to 17,649 with 9 deaths. In response, the Tamil Nadu Department of Public Health urges heightened vigilance in high-transmission areas and advises that patients, pregnant women, the elderly, those with weakened immunity, and children wear masks to curb spread. State and municipal field workers are conducting door-to-door vector-control and other fever-prevention measures across households. Authorities emphasize prompt hospital care for fever or related symptoms and advise keeping children home from school if they have fever. Residents are urged to prevent water stagnation inside homes to reduce mosquito breeding. The article does not provide details on laboratory confirmation or any imported/exported cases.

triage.headline_ja: 「これらの人々はマスク着用が必要」―デング熱の拡大を防ぐための重要な助言
triage.triage_reason: インド・タミルナドゥ州でのデング熱は例年発生する風土病であり、異常性・国際拡大リスクは低いが、死亡者数（9名）と感染者数（17,649件）の規模から経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: デング熱はインドで毎年季節的に発生する風土病であり、本記事は州政府による予防啓発が中心。感染規模・死亡数は一定程度あるが、国際的な異常事象とは言えないため、フルRRAではなく経過観察とする。

article.articleHeadline: Vaiolo scimmie: confusione su test, un terzo sarebbe falso positivo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Monkeypox: confusion over tests, a third would be a false positive.
article.articleSummary: One-third of PCR tests for monkeypox (Mpox) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo may be false positives, according to an international study led by the University of Geneva and published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. Analyzing over 2,700 samples from four cities, researchers found positives split into two groups: a majority with high viral load confirming infection, and about 35% with only trace viral DNA, likely due to environmental contamination. Investigations at two treatment centers detected Mpox DNA on surfaces, suggesting sample carryover. Blood analyses showed lack of antibodies in 89% of individuals flagged as falsely positive, while their rashes could be due to measles or varicella, the researchers note. False positives led to unnecessary hospitalisation or isolation and could distort epidemiological monitoring and vaccination planning. Authors recommend confirming positives with higher viral load thresholds and improving laboratory training to recognize anomalous test patterns.

triage.headline_ja: サル痘（Mpox）：検査に混乱、陽性の3分の1が偽陽性の可能性
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国におけるMpox（クレードI含む）のPCR検査で約3分の1が偽陽性である可能性が示され、既存のMpox流行（PHEIC相当）のサーベイランスやワクチン戦略に影響を及ぼす重大な公衆衛生上の懸念であるため、フルリスク評価が必要と判断する。
triage.notes: 本記事はジュネーブ大学主導の国際研究（The Lancet Infectious Diseases掲載）に基づき、DRCのMpox検査における偽陽性問題を指摘するもの。既存の流行地域における検査精度・サーベイランス体制の信頼性に関わる重要な知見であり、今後の対応方針（隔離・ワクチン計画等）への影響を評価する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: East African Community (EAC) Steps Up Regional Infectious Disease Outbreak Preparedness, Calls for More Support
article.articleSummary: East African Community (EAC) strengthens preparedness for high-consequence infectious diseases. In Nairobi, 120 health professionals from eight Partner States are undergoing training under the Training in the East African Community for High-Consequence Infectious Diseases (tEACh) programme, with workshops through November 2026. Delivered by Charité Berlin and East African clinicians trained through tEACh, the programme builds a pool of clinicians to detect, manage, and train colleagues across Partner States. A Mobile Laboratory Network now comprises 10 labs across seven States (Beni, Busia, Nimule-Elegu, Kobero, Bwera), enabling rapid diagnostics at strategic sites and entry points and supporting responses to Ebola, Marburg, COVID-19 and Mpox; expansion to 34 labs is planned by end-2027. Needs total USD 45 million; Germany pledges €4.8 million to scale Ebola preparedness, fund training for 500 workers, sensitise 15,000 people in eastern DRC, provide 20,000 PPE sets, and support vaccine registration pending WHO approval.

triage.headline_ja: 東アフリカ共同体（EAC）、地域感染症アウトブレイク対応能力を強化、追加支援を要請
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はEAC地域における感染症対応の訓練・体制強化・資金支援に関するプレスリリースであり、具体的な感染症の発生・流行を報告するものではないため、トリアージ基準に該当しない。
triage.notes: 記事はEBS/Ebola/Marburg/COVID-19/Mpoxへの備え強化に関する能力構築プログラム（訓練・検査室ネットワーク・資金調達）についての報道であり、特定の疾病アウトブレイクの発生を報じるものではない。東部DRCへの支援言及はあるが、実際の発生確認情報ではないため verified_locations には含めない。

article.articleHeadline: 安特羅與泰國 Biogenetech 簽訂經銷合約 布局泰國腸病毒EV71疫苗市場
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Antro and Thailand-based Biogenetech Sign Distribution Agreement to Establish a Foothold in Thailand's EV71 Enterovirus Vaccine Market.
article.articleSummary: Antro Biotech, part of Guoguang Biotech Group, signed an exclusive Thailand distribution agreement with Biogenetech to bring the enterovirus 71 (EV71) vaccine to Thailand. The plan targets about 3 million infants in self-pay and government tender markets. Biogenetech, a Thailand-based firm with 30+ years of experience, operates an established nationwide cold-chain network and direct access to major public/private hospitals; its public tender track record includes rabies vaccine capturing over 30% market share within two years. Antro expects Biogenetech’s logistics and tender strengths to accelerate Thai regulatory listing and market launch of the EV71 vaccine. EV71 is highly neurotropic and can cause encephalitis and cardiopulmonary failure. Official data show Thailand had 94,670 HFMD cases in Jan–Sep 2025, with EV71 comprising 18–19% of tested samples. The 0–4 age group is about 2.64 million, with ~400,000 births annually; NDA with Thai FDA was filed in Aug 2025.

triage.headline_ja: 安特羅とタイBiogenetech社が販売代理契約を締結、タイのEV71腸病毒ワクチン市場へ布局
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はワクチンの販売代理契約に関する企業ビジネス情報であり、新規の感染症発生や公衆衛生上の緊急事態を報告するものではない。
triage.notes: 記事はHFMD/EV71ワクチンの市場参入・販売契約に関する経済ニュースであり、疾患の異常発生や流行拡大を報じるものではない。タイの2025年1-9月のHFMD統計は背景情報として引用されているのみ。

article.articleHeadline: Kasus ISPA & Flu di Surabaya Naik 15 Persen Saat Puncak Kemarau, Dinkes Minta Warga Lebih Waspada
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cases of Upper Respiratory Tract Infections (URTIs) and Flu in Surabaya Rise 15 Percent During the Peak of the Dry Season, Health Department Urges Residents to Be More Vigilant
article.articleSummary: Surabaya, Indonesia—The Surabaya City Health Department reports a 10–15% rise in acute respiratory infections (ARIs) and influenza entering September 2026, the peak of the dry season, versus January–August 2026 (data through week 3). The uptick is currently controlled: no inpatient admissions and health facilities able to handle patients. Influenza A symptoms resemble a common flu and have low fatality; treatment follows standard flu care, with no need for extensive strain-specific measures. Most patients seek outpatient care at clinics or primary health centers. Residents are urged to stay vigilant but avoid panic, maintain rest and a balanced diet, and consider vitamin C. Mask use is advised in crowds or enclosed spaces. Influenza vaccination is available at nearby health facilities as an additional preventive measure.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The contagious disease that hit Ronaldinho and his entourage, what is 'Yellow Fever'?
article.articleSummary: Ronaldinho and members of his entourage were detained at Kochi airport for not presenting Yellow Fever vaccination certificates before entering India for the Return of the Titans series; entry was allowed after presenting a digital certificate. Yellow Fever is a mosquito-borne viral disease, found mainly in Africa and tropical Americas; most infections are mild, but severe disease can cause liver and kidney failure and bleeding, with a case-fatality rate of 30-60% in severe cases. There is no specific antiviral treatment, but a single-dose vaccine provides long-lasting protection; international certificates become valid 10 days after vaccination. At-risk regions include Angola, Nigeria, Ghana, Uganda, Cameroon, DR Congo, and in the Americas Brazil, Colombia, Peru, Bolivia, and Venezuela. Kerala faces heightened risk due to high Aedes aegypti density; past Zika virus was reported in Thiruvananthapuram in 2022. Emphasized are travel health checks, vector control, disease surveillance, and public awareness to prevent cross-border spread.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A doctor recommended that tourists from Thailand undergo a test if they have COVID-19 symptoms - News on Vesti.ru.
article.articleSummary: Tourists returning from Thailand to Russia may bring COVID-19, with spread depending on how quickly the pathogen is localized and on potential changes in the virus. Moscow-based infectious disease physician Georgiy Vikulov told NEWS.ru that travelers with COVID-19 symptoms during or after travel should not self-medicate, but urgently seek medical evaluation. Molecular diagnostics can rapidly identify the exact pathogen or pathogens, and co-infections are possible, guiding appropriate treatment. Tests can be performed outside clinics in network laboratories; rapid tests exist that can simultaneously detect COVID-19, influenza, and other respiratory agents. Vikulov noted that infection can progress with few or no symptoms in people with greater resistance. Previously, Russian tour operators did not warn travelers about COVID-19 risk in Thailand and did not cancel already paid trips.

article.articleHeadline: Four north districts in Tamil Nadu on alert amid spike in dengue cases
article.articleSummary: Four north Tamil Nadu districts—Vellore, Ranipet, Tiruvannamalai and Tirupattur—on heightened watch after a dengue spike. Ranipet has recorded 59 dengue cases since September 1, with 14 fresh cases in the week of September 14–20, averaging two to four new cases daily. In Vellore, 10 dengue cases were reported in September and 15 in August; all 10 cases this month have been discharged, with two to three cases per week on average and ongoing intensive monitoring. With neighboring districts reporting higher activity, authorities are tightening vigilance, including college hostel inspections, intensive fogging by domestic breeding checkers, and chlorination. Fever patients are being screened and dengue cases segregated from leptospirosis, scrub typhus, and chikungunya. Officials say rises after the monsoon are a typical seasonal pattern and vigilant surveillance continues.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 15-minute dengue home audit: Make sure your home isn’t a haven for mosquitoes; follow these simple precautions.
article.articleSummary: Dengue outbreaks are rising in several Indian cities, with Aedes mosquitoes (Aedes aegypti) breeding in small amounts of water around homes and apartments. Mosquitoes bite mainly during the day, especially after sunrise and before sunset. A 15-minute, twice-daily home audit is advised: inspect plant pot saucers and trays, fridge drip trays, AC condensation leaks, cooler water tanks, balcony planters, and water-collecting surfaces; seal any water-holding containers and fit mesh on overflow pipes and water tanks. Keep toilets dry, drain and flush weekly, and ensure floors are dry; check stairs, basements, sump rooms, and generator rooms for standing water. Maintain a no-standing-water habit and set reminders for morning and evening checks. Dengue warning signs typically appear 3–7 days after fever onset; alarm features include vomiting, severe abdominal pain, gum or nasal bleeding, extreme weakness, confusion, or fluid accumulation in chest/abdomen, with rising hematocrit and falling platelets—seek emergency care. If mosquitoes persist, report to municipal vector control for fogging or insecticide spraying (temephos or Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis at 1 ppm) and keep water tanks mesh-covered.

article.articleHeadline: WHO: Wabah ebola di RD Kongo belum terkendali
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: Ebola outbreak in the DR Congo not yet under control.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo remains uncontrolled as of 20 September 2026, with 7,733 lab-confirmed cases and 3,732 deaths, per the WHO Africa Regional Office. The outbreak is spreading geographically, now affecting 63 health zones across seven provinces and extending toward the South Sudan border in Dungu, Haut-Uele Province, raising cross-border transmission risk. Health-system strain is highest in North Kivu, where standard Ebola care facilities are 91.2% full and 34.2% of hospitalized patients receive care outside standard facilities. Community deaths remain a major concern, underscoring delays in detection, referral, and access to care. WHO assesses the risk of further spread within DR Congo as very high and cross-border risk as high. Declared in May, it is the largest Ebola outbreak in DR Congo and the second largest globally after 2014–2016 West Africa. The article provides no infection-source or imported/exported-case details.

article.articleHeadline: อุทาหรณ์คนทำสวน! หญิงวัย 65 เดินเท้าเปล่าย่ำดิน ถูก "พยาธิชอนไช" คันเกาจนติดเชื้อลุกลาม
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A warning to gardeners! A 65-year-old woman walking barefoot on soil contracted a burrowing parasite ('hookworm') that caused itching from scratching and led to a spreading infection.
article.articleSummary: 65-year-old woman in Thailand with diabetes and hypertension developed creeping eruption (cutaneous larva migrans) after walking barefoot in a soursop orchard. She presented with blistering, inflamed foot lesions that progressed to purulent discharge within a day despite antibiotics. Examination revealed serpiginous, reddish tracks consistent with skin-penetrating nematode larvae. The infection was caused by hookworm larvae from dog/cat feces—or Strongyloides—in soil. In this patient, diabetes and marked pruritus led to scratching and secondary bacterial infection (Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes) in the dermis. The condition is not life-threatening; larvae remain in the epidermis as incidental hosts and typically die over weeks. Treatment included oral anthelmintic Albendazole 400 mg daily for 3–7 days, antihistamines, and a short course of topical steroids; antibiotics such as Dicloxacillin or Cephalexin, plus topical mupirocin or fusidic acid for infected skin. Prevention: avoid barefoot exposure.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : la Tunisie envoie une cargaison d'aide médicale vers la RDC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Tunisia Sends a Shipment of Medical Aid to the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) persists as Tunisia dispatches a major medical aid shipment on 22 September 2026 to support Congolese authorities amid an epidemic. The cargo comprises medications and medical and paramedical equipment, intended to bolster the response; the delivery will be coordinated through the Tunisian Embassy in Kinshasa. According to WHO’s weekly report up to 20 September 2026, the DRC has 7,733 confirmed Ebola cases and 3,732 deaths since the start of the outbreak. The epidemic continues to spread to new areas, with the virus approaching international borders; Dungu health zone in Haut-Uélé near the South Sudan border is the latest affected area. In total, 63 health zones across seven provinces are affected. WHO maintains the national risk as very high and neighboring-country risk as high; the outbreak is the largest and deadliest in the DRC and second-largest globally after 2014–2016 West Africa.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cases of Acute Respiratory Infections (ARI) and Influenza in Surabaya Rise 10-15 Percent in September 2026, Health Office Urges Residents Not to Panic.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A and acute respiratory infections (ARI) in Surabaya rose by 10–15% in September 2026 during the peak dry season, though the health office says the situation remains under control and urges calm. Surabaya Health Office reports increases compared with January–August 2026, with data up to the third week of September 2026. No hospitalizations or bed shortages were observed; facilities including RSUD dr. Mohammad Soewandhie and RSUD Eka Candrarini remain sufficient, and most patients seek outpatient care at clinics or Puskesmas. Infections are generally mild; Influenza A presents flu-like symptoms with low fatality, and extensive genomic strain differentiation is not deemed necessary. Preventive measures include rest, balanced nutrition, vitamin C, mask use in crowds or enclosed spaces, and influenza vaccination at local health facilities. Symptomatic individuals with cough, fever, or weakness should rest and visit Puskesmas if symptoms persist. Nationally, influenza positivity was 46% in week 37 (Kemenkes).

article.articleHeadline: The World Forgot About Ebola. The Organization Fighting It Has Never Been More Worried
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Bundibugyo Ebola virus outbreak has surpassed 7,000 cases and about 3,500 deaths since May, marking it as one of the fastest-growing Ebola epidemics in recent memory. Uganda previously contained a Bundibugyo outbreak via contact tracing and isolation, but DRC’s instability and mass displacement hinder surveillance and safe burial, while distrust of outside humanitarian workers complicates containment. Vaccine development has accelerated: CEPI redirected $100 million to fund Oxford University’s ChAdOx1 BDBV vaccine (manufactured by Serum Institute of India) and Moderna’s candidate; safety trials are underway and efficacy trials are expected this month. Experts warn vaccine distrust could undermine containment. With funding gaps, CEPI could run out by December without new commitments. The US and partners support enhanced surveillance, diagnostics, travel screening, and border health activities in coordination with the DRC and Uganda.

article.articleHeadline: Đầu năm học mới, cha mẹ nhớ làm việc này để phòng viêm não Nhật Bản cho con
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: At the start of the new school year, parents should do this to protect their child from Japanese encephalitis.
article.articleSummary: Japanese encephalitis, a mosquito-borne viral disease, is particularly a concern in Vietnam as the school year begins and rainy, warm weather create more Culex mosquito activity. Initial symptoms include fever, headache, nausea; severe cases may lead to lethargy, seizures, and altered consciousness, with risk of long-term neurological or cognitive impairment. WHO notes there is no specific antiviral treatment; care is supportive, and fatality among symptomatic cases can reach about 30%, with 20–30% of survivors incurring lasting sequelae. Vietnam’s Expanded Program on Immunization uses three primary JEV doses: at age 1 year (dose 1), 1–2 weeks later (dose 2), and one year after dose 1 (dose 3). Booster doses are recommended every 3 years until age 15. Parents should check vaccination records, ensure boosters are up to date, and combine immunization with mosquito control measures (bed nets, long clothing, removing standing water). If records are missing, consult a vaccination center for a tailored schedule.

article.articleHeadline: Afrique : l'EAC chiffre à 45 millions USD ses besoins pour renforcer sa capacité de riposte aux épidémies des maladies infectieuses dans la région
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Africa: the EAC estimates its needs at 45 million USD to strengthen its capacity to respond to outbreaks of infectious diseases in the region.
article.articleSummary: As of 23 September 2026, the East African Community (EAC) estimates $45 million in resources to strengthen partner states' capacity to prevent and manage Ebola outbreaks and other viral hemorrhagic fevers. The plan accelerates epidemic preparedness across eight EAC states, aiming to shorten detection and containment times and mitigate cross-border economic impacts. German support comprises €4.8 million to train 500 frontline health workers, run awareness campaigns for 15,000 people in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, and procure 20,000 PPE kits, plus backing for Ebola vaccine registration in partner states, including the Bundibugyo virus, pending WHO approval. A parallel push expands diagnostic capacity from 10 mobile labs in seven states (positions including Beni, Busia, Nimule-Elegu, Kobero, Bwera) to 34 by end-2027. Training under tEACh, via GIZ and Aga Khan Centre, links regional capacity to cross-border health security and economic resilience.

article.articleHeadline: Congo-Kinshasa: Ebola, choléra, rougeole, conflits armés - Des systèmes de santé fragilisés par ces multiples crises
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo: Ebola, cholera, measles, armed conflicts — health systems weakened by these multiple crises.
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Ebola response strains a health system already battling cholera and measles amid ongoing conflict. The Health Cluster warns these emergencies rely on the same personnel, vehicles, laboratories, and medicines, a situation worsened by funding shortfalls. By early September, cholera had generated over 43,000 suspected cases and 1,050 deaths since the start of the year, while measles topped 120,000 suspected cases and 1,600 deaths, with nearly eight in ten patients under five. The Ebola response absorbs essential resources—staff, labs, surveillance, and stock—needed for the other diseases. As of August 31, less than half of the $2.13 billion humanitarian appeal had been funded. Authorities warn that concentrating on Ebola risks receding vaccination, deliveries, maternal care, mental health, and care for sexual violence survivors. They urge explicit protection of non-Ebola services, secured drug stocks, and coordinated funding to contain Ebola without collapsing essential health services.

triage.notes: エボラ単独ではなく、コレラ・はしか・紛争が複合し保健システムの崩壊リスクを高めている点が重要。資金不足（appeal未達）が国際支援必要性を裏付ける。

article.articleHeadline: Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC): Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) expands response to Ebola disease with new treatment centres as outbreak spreads across provinces
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo (Ituri and Tshopo provinces) expands as Nia Nia–linked transmission reaches Kisangani. MSF has added two new ETcs: in Kisangani at Hôpital du Cinquantenaire a 22-bed centre opened in early September to augment an existing facility; in Nia Nia, a new 50-bed ETC opened beside the local hospital (16 beds for suspected cases, 34 for confirmed). As of 1 September 2026, Nia Nia ETC admitted 85 people with symptoms matching Ebola; 59 were confirmed, including 15 deaths. In Kisangani, 14 positive cases were recorded by 1 September, with 13 having an epidemiological link to Nia Nia. The outbreak is driven by movement between Ituri, Tshopo and Haut-Uele; infections in Kisangani include cases linked to a body arriving from Nia Nia, and three Nia Nia-linked patients died in Kisangani last week. MSF underscores that surveillance, testing, contact tracing, IPC, isolation, and community engagement are essential alongside treatment capacity.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国（DRC）：国境なき医師団（MSF）、複数州に拡大するエボラ流行に対応し新たな治療センターを増設
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がイトゥリ・チョポ両州にまたがり拡大し、確定例・死亡例が継続的に報告されているため、IHR基準（深刻性・異常性）を満たしフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: Nia Nia起点の感染連鎖がキサンガニ（州都）にまで拡大し、遺体搬送や患者移動による地域間伝播が確認されている。MSFが治療センターを増設し対応中で、監視・接触者追跡・地域社会エンゲージメントの強化が課題とされる。

article.articleHeadline: Wabak Ebola di DR Congo masih tidak terkawal - WHO
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo remains out of control - WHO
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo remains out of control, according to the WHO. As of 23 September 2026, 7,733 confirmed cases and 3,732 deaths have been reported by the WHO Africa Regional Office. Transmission has moved into a new area: Dungu health zone, Haut-Uele Province, on the border with South Sudan, raising cross-border spillover risk. The outbreak now affects 63 health zones across seven provinces. In North Kivu, Ebola treatment center occupancy stands at 91.2%, with 34.2% of patients treated outside designated facilities. Community deaths remain a major concern, with nearly two-thirds of confirmed deaths last week occurring outside treatment facilities due to delays in detection, referral, and access to care. WHO assesses spillover risk as very high for DRC and high for neighboring land-border countries. Declared in May, it is the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in DRC, and second-largest globally after 2014–2016 West Africa.

triage.headline_ja: DRCのエボラ出血熱流行、依然として制御不能 - WHO
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模（世界2番目）のエボラ流行が継続中で、南スーダン国境地帯への拡大とスピルオーバーリスクの上昇が確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: 南スーダン(Republic of the Sudan)は対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていないが、国境地帯での感染拡大・スピルオーバーリスクの観点から続報を要注視。

article.articleHeadline: Angola soma mais 19 casos de Mpox nas últimas 24 horas
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Angola reports 19 more Mpox cases in the last 24 hours.
article.articleSummary: Angola reports 19 new mpox (monkeypox) cases in the last 24 hours, raising the total to 615 with 107 active. New infections are in Moxico East (5), Luanda (5), Cabinda (3), Moxico (2), Huambo (1), Icolo and Bengo (1), Namibe (1), and Uíge (1). Four recoveries (three in Moxico East, one in Cabinda). The Ministry of Health has reactivated the National Contingency Plan (initiated July) to detect suspected cases, confirm infections, identify contacts, and monitor spread amid border concerns with the DRC. Mpox is caused by a monkeypox virus; incubation 5–21 days; symptoms include fever, headache, fatigue, muscle pain, lymphadenopathy, and generalized skin rash. Preventive measures: hand hygiene, avoid hunting/eating primates or rodents, avoid contact with symptomatic people and contaminated materials, and protective handling of animals. The clade 1b lineage was detected in DRC in September 2023; WHO has declared mpox a global emergency; transmission is via close contact.

triage.headline_ja: アンゴラ、過去24時間でMpox感染者が19人増加
triage.triage_reason: アンゴラでクレードib系統のMpoxが継続的に拡大しており、WHOがPHEICを宣言した疾患であること、また国境を接するDRCとの越境拡大懸念があることからIHR基準を2つ以上満たすためフルリスク評価に進めるべきと判断した。
